/* global define:false */
define(["lodash", "jquery", "app/config"], function (_, $, Config) {
  "use strict";

  var KEY_MAP = Config.get("general.keyMap");
  var KEY_DISPLAY_GROUPS = Config.get("general.keyDisplayGroups");
  var KEY_SIGNATURE_MAP = Config.get("general.keySignatureMap");

  var KeySignatureWidget = function (keySignature, settings) {
    this.settings = settings || {};
    this.settings = _.merge(
      {
        widgetCls: "widget-keysignature widget-keysignature-header",
        lockedCls: "ioncustom-siglocked",
        unlockedCls: "ioncustom-sigunlocked",
      },
      settings
    );
    this.lock = keySignature.locked();
    this.keySignature = keySignature;
    this.el = $('<div class="' + this.settings.widgetCls + '"></div>');
    this.initListeners();
  };

  _.extend(KeySignatureWidget.prototype, {
    // initialize event listeners
    initListeners: function () {
      var that = this;

      // delegate change events on the root element
      this.el.on("change", function (e) {
        var target = e.target;
        if (target === that.keyEl[0]) {
          that.keySignature.changeKey($(target).val(), that.lock);
          that.render();
        } else if (target === that.signatureEl[0]) {
          that.keySignature.changeSignatureKey($(target).val(), that.lock);
          that.render();
        }
      });
      this.el.on("click", function (e) {
        var target = e.target;
        if (target == that.lockEl[0]) {
          that._updateSignatureLock();
          that.keySignature.changeSignatureLock(that.lock);
        }
      });

      // observe changes to key signature and refresh when needed
      this.keySignature.bind("change", function () {
        that.lock = this.locked();
        that.render();
      });
    },
    // render the control elements
    render: function () {
      this._renderKeySelector();
      this._renderSignatureLock();
      this._renderSignatureSelector();
      this.el.empty();
      this.el.append(this.keyEl, this.lockContainerEl, this.signatureEl);
      return this;
    },
    // renders the lock checkbox that is used to bind the key and signature
    // together (change one and the other should change accordingly).
    _renderSignatureLock: function () {
      var lock = this.lock ? true : false;
      var lockCls = [
        "btn ion-locked " + this.settings.lockedCls,
        "btn ion-unlocked " + this.settings.unlockedCls,
      ];
      var lockContainerEl = $("<span/>");
      var lockEl = $(
        '<span title="Toggle lock of key and staff signature" class="' +
          (lock ? lockCls[0] : lockCls[1]) +
          '" data-lock="' +
          (lock ? "yes" : "no") +
          '"/>'
      );
      var style = 'style="margin: 0 10px"';

      lockContainerEl.append(lockEl);

      this.lockCls = lockCls;
      this.lockEl = lockEl;
      this.lockContainerEl = lockContainerEl;

      return this;
    },
    // updates the signature lock based on the value of the
    _updateSignatureLock: function () {
      var lockCls = this.lockCls.slice(0);

      this.lock = this.lockEl.data("lock") == "yes" ? false : true;
      if (this.lock) {
        lockCls.reverse();
      }
      this.lockEl.removeClass(lockCls[0]).addClass(lockCls[1]);
      this.lockEl.data("lock", this.lock ? "yes" : "no");
    },
    // renders a selectable list of signatures
    _renderSignatureSelector: function () {
      var select = document.createElement("select");
      select.name = "keysignature";
      var selected_signature = this.keySignature.getSignatureSpec();

      _.each(KEY_SIGNATURE_MAP, function (majorKey, signature) {
        var option = document.createElement("option");
        option.text = signature === "" ? "No staff signature" : signature;
        // .replace(/b/g,'♭').replace(/#/g,'♯')
        option.value = majorKey;
        if (signature === selected_signature) {
          option.selected = true;
        }
        select.appendChild(option);
      });

      this.signatureEl = $(select);
      return this;
    },
    // renders a selectable list of keys
    _renderKeySelector: function () {
      var select = document.createElement("select");
      select.name = "key";
      var selected_key = this.keySignature.getKey();

      _.each(KEY_DISPLAY_GROUPS, function (keyList, index) {
        var optgroup = document.createElement("optgroup");
        optgroup.label = keyList[0];

        _.each(keyList.slice(1), function (key, index) {
          var opt = document.createElement("option");
          opt.value = key;
          opt.text = KEY_MAP[key].name;
          if (key === selected_key) {
            opt.selected = true;
          }
          optgroup.appendChild(opt);
        });

        select.appendChild(optgroup);
      });

      this.keyEl = $(select);
      return this;
    },
  });

  return KeySignatureWidget;
});

lab/static/js/src/widgets/theme_selector.js
File type: .js
define(["jquery", "lodash"], function ($, _) {
  var ThemeSelectorWidget = function (targetEl) {
    this.el = $('<ul class="theme-thumbnails"></ul>');
    this.targetEl = $(targetEl); // set theme on this el
    this.themes = []; // available themes
    _.bindAll(this, ["onSelectTheme"]);
  };

  _.extend(ThemeSelectorWidget.prototype, {
    init: function () {
      if (this.targetEl.data("themes")) {
        this.themes = this.targetEl.data("themes").split(",");
      }
      this.initListeners();
    },
    initListeners: function () {
      this.el.delegate(".theme-thumbnail", "click", this.onSelectTheme);
    },
    onSelectTheme: function (ev) {
      var theme_key = "theme";
      var prefix = "theme-";
      var $el = $(ev.target);
      var old_theme = this.targetEl.data(theme_key);
      var new_theme = $el.data(theme_key);

      if (new_theme !== old_theme) {
        this.targetEl.removeClass(prefix + old_theme);
        this.targetEl.addClass(prefix + new_theme);
        this.targetEl.data(theme_key, new_theme);

        // force update of data attribute in DOM as well
        this.targetEl[0].setAttribute("data-" + theme_key, new_theme);
      }
      return false;
    },
    render: function () {
      this.el.html("");

      var els = _.map(
        this.themes,
        function (name) {
          var el = $("<li/>");
          el[0].className = ["theme-thumbnail", "theme-" + name].join(" ");
          el[0].setAttribute("data-theme", name);
          return el;
        },
        this
      );

      this.el.append(els);

      return this;
    },
  });

  return ThemeSelectorWidget;
});

        this.trigger("changeOption", "highlight", opt, this.state.mode[opt]);
      },
      highlight_doublings: function (e) {
        var opt = e.target.value;
        this.state.mode[opt] = e.target.checked;
        this.trigger("changeOption", "highlight", opt, this.state.mode[opt]);

      highlight_solobass: function (e) {
        var opt = e.target.value;
        this.state.mode[opt] = e.target.checked;
        this.trigger("changeOption", "highlight", opt, this.state.mode[opt]);
      },
    },
    render: function () {
      var that = this;

      // update the element content
      if (this.is_exercise_view) {
        this.el.html(
          this.templateHTML.replace(
            /type="checkbox"/gi,
            'type="checkbox" onclick="return false;"'
          )
        );
      } else {
        this.el.html(this.templateHTML);
      }

      // update the input states
      this.el.find("input[name=highlight_enabled]")[0].checked =
        this.state.enabled;
      $.each(this.state.mode, function (key, val) {
        var $input = that.el.find("input[value=" + key + "]");
        $input.attr("checked", val ? true : false);
        $input.attr("disabled", !that.state.enabled);
      });

      return this;
    },
    getState: function () {
      return this.state;
    },
  });

  MicroEvent.mixin(HighlightWidget);

  return HighlightWidget;
});

        var $input = that.el.find("input[value=" + key + "]");
        $input.attr("checked", val ? true : false);
        $input.attr("disabled", !that.state.enabled);
      });

      // set the "neither" option
      if (!this._eitherModeTrue("note_names", "scientific_pitch")) {
        this.el
          .find("input[value=neither][name=note_analysis]")
          .attr("checked", true)
          .attr("disabled", !this.state.enabled);
      }
      // if (!this._eitherModeTrue('scale_degrees', 'solfege')) {
      // 	this.el.find('input[value=neither][name=melodic_analysis]').attr('checked', true).attr('disabled', !this.state.enabled);
      // }

      return this;
    },
    getState: function () {
      return this.state;
    },
    _eitherModeTrue: function (a, b) {
      return this.state.mode[a] || this.state.mode[b];
    },
  });

  MicroEvent.mixin(AnalyzeWidget);

  return AnalyzeWidget;
});

lab/static/js/src/widgets/staff_distribute.js
File type: .js
/* global define:false */
define(["lodash", "jquery", "microevent", "app/config"], function (
  _,
  $,
  MicroEvent,
  Config
) {
  "use strict";

  const VALID_STAFF_DISTRIBUTIONS = Config.get(
    "general.validStaffDistributions"
  );
  var STAFF_DISTRIBUTION = Config.get("general.staffDistribution");

  if (false) {
    sessionStorage.removeItem("staffDistribution"); // retire this function
  } else {
    var storage_staff_dist = sessionStorage.getItem("staffDistribution");
    if (
      storage_staff_dist &&
      VALID_STAFF_DISTRIBUTIONS.includes(storage_staff_dist)
    ) {
      STAFF_DISTRIBUTION = storage_staff_dist;
    }
  }

  var StaffDistributionWidget = function (
    distribution = false,
    is_exercise_view = false
  ) {
    this.is_exercise_view = is_exercise_view || false;
    this.el = $('<div class="menu-widgets"></div>');
    this.state =
      distribution && VALID_STAFF_DISTRIBUTIONS.includes(distribution)
        ? distribution
        : STAFF_DISTRIBUTION;
    this.init();
  };

  var staff_distribution_labels = {
    // compare dashboard
    "keyboard": "Keyboard* or break solo lines at B4, C4",
    "keyboardPlusLHBias": "Keyboard* or break solo lines above F4",
    "keyboardPlusRHBias": "Keyboard* or break solo lines below G3",
    "chorale": "Chorale or break solo lines at B4, C4",
    "grandStaff": "Break at B4, C4",
    "LH": "Lower staff only, legible through G4",
    "RH": "Upper staff only, legible through F3",
  }

  _.extend(StaffDistributionWidget.prototype, {
    templateHTML:
      [
        '<fieldset class="settings-notation">',
        "<legend><label>STAFF DISTRIBUTION</label></legend>",
        "<ul>",
      ].join("") +
      VALID_STAFF_DISTRIBUTIONS.map((opt) =>
        [
          '<li><label><input type="checkbox" name="staff_distribution" value="',
          opt,
          '"> ',
          staff_distribution_labels[opt],
          "</label></li>",
        ].join("")
      ).join("") +
      [
        "</ul>",
        "<p>*SAT no lower than G3, bass no higher than F3</p>",
        "</fieldset>"
      ].join(""),
    init: function () {
      this.initListeners();
    },
    initListeners: function () {
      var that = this;
      this.el.on("change", "input", null, function (e) {
        var target_name = e.target.name;
        if (target_name in that.handlers) {
          that.handlers[target_name].call(that, e);
        }
        e.stopPropagation();
      });
    },
    handlers: {
      staff_distribution: function (e) {
        var opt = e.target.value; // e.g. "keyboard"
        this.state = opt;
        /* temporary hack */
        sessionStorage.setItem("staffDistribution", opt);
        if (e.target.checked) {
          this.trigger("changeValue", "distribute", opt);
        }
        this.render();
      },
    },
    render: function () {
      var that = this;

      if (this.is_exercise_view) {
        this.el.html(
          this.templateHTML.replace(
            /type="checkbox"/gi,
            'type="checkbox" onclick="return false;"'
          )
        );
      } else {
        this.el.html(this.templateHTML);
      }

      // update the input states
      $.each(VALID_STAFF_DISTRIBUTIONS, function (idx, val) {
        var $input = that.el.find("input[value=" + val + "]");
        $input.attr("checked", val == that.state ? true : false);
      });

      return this;
    },
    getState: function () {
      return this.state;
    },
  });

  MicroEvent.mixin(StaffDistributionWidget);

  return StaffDistributionWidget;
});

lab/static/js/src/widgets/modal.js
File type: .js
/* global define:false */
define(["lodash", "jquery"], function (_, $) {
  "use strict";

  /**
   * Defines the html template.
   * @type {function}
   * @const
   */
  var MODAL_TPL = _.template(
    [
      '<div class="modal-wrapper">',
      '<a href="#" class="modal-close-btn js-modal-close-btn">x</a>',
      '<h2 class="modal-title"><%= title %></h2>',
      '<div class="modal-body"><%= msg %><div>',
      "</div>",
    ].join("")
  );

  /**
   * Creates an instance of a modal dialog.
   *
   * Only one modal dialog may be active at a time.
   *
   * This is *not* intended to be a feature-complete modal dialog, just a
   * simple dialog to display a message to the user. If something more complex
   * is needed, get a jQuery plugin or other ready-made component.
   *
   * @constructor
   * @param {object} config
   */
  var Modal = function (config) {
    _.bindAll(this, ["onClose", "onClickOutsideModal"]);
    this.init(config);
  };

  /**
   * Adds a modal dialog to the list.
   *
   * @param {Modal} modal
   * @return undefined
   */
  Modal.add = function (modal) {
    this.modals = this.modals || [];
    this.modals.push(modal);
  };

  /**
   * Closes all modals.
   *
   * @return undefined
   */
  Modal.closeAll = function () {
    _.invoke(this.modals, "close");
  };

  /**
   * Destroys all active modals.
   *
   * @return undefined
   */
  Modal.destroyAll = function () {
    _.invoke(this.modals, "destroy");
    this.modals = [];
  };

  _.extend(Modal.prototype, {
    /**
     * Initializes the modal dialog.
     *
     * @param {object} config
     * @param {string} config.title
     * @param {string} config.msg
     * @return undefinefd
     */
    init: function (config) {
      this.title = config.title;
      this.msg = config.msg;
      this.el = $('<div class="modal close"></div>');
      Modal.add(this);
    },
    /**
     * Renders the dialog.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    render: function () {
      var html = MODAL_TPL({ title: this.title, msg: this.msg });
      this.el.html(html);
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Initializes listeners.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    initListeners: function () {
      this.el.on("click", ".js-modal-close-btn", null, this.onClose);
      $("body").on("click", this.onClickOutsideModal);
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Removes listeners.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    removeListeners: function () {
      this.el.unbind("click", ".js-modal-close-btn", null, this.onClose);
      $("body").unbind("click", this.onClickOutsideModal);
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Opens the dialog.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    open: function () {
      this.render().appendToDOM();
      this.initListeners();
      this.el.removeClass("close").addClass("open");
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Handles the close event.
     *
     * @param evt
     * @return undefined
     */
    onClose: function (evt) {
      evt.preventDefault();
      this.close();
    },
    /**
     * Closes the modal if a click is detected outside the modal
     *
     * @return undefined
     */
    onClickOutsideModal: function (evt) {
      evt.preventDefault();
      if ($(".modal").find(evt.target).length == 0) {
        this.close();
      }
    },
    /**
     * Closes the dialog.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    close: function () {
      this.el.removeClass("open").addClass("close");
      this.removeListeners();
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Destroys the dialog.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    destroy: function () {
      this.removeListeners();
      this.el.remove();
      return this;
    },
    /**
     * Appends the modal dialog to the DOM.
     *
     * @return this
     */
    appendToDOM: function () {
      if (!this.appendedToDom) {
        $("body").append(this.el);
        this.appendedToDom = true;
      }
      return this;
    },
  });

  /**
   * Shortcut method to display simple modal dialog
   *
   * @static
   * @param {string} title
   * @param {string} msg
   * @return {Modal} The modal dialog object.
   */
  Modal.msg = function (title, msg) {
    var cacheKey = title + msg;
    Modal.cache = Modal.cache || {};
    if (Modal.cache[cacheKey]) {
      Modal.cache[cacheKey].open();
    } else {
      var modal = new Modal({ title: title, msg: msg });
      Modal.closeAll();
      modal.open();
      Modal.cache[cacheKey] = modal;
    }
  };

  return Modal;
});

  <div id="analysis-output" style="font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; white-space: pre; line-height: 1.4;"></div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

docs/exercise_types.md
File type: .md
# Exercise Types

HarmonyLab has two fundamental interaction modes:

| Mode | Student action | Examples |
|------|---------------|---------|
| **Play** | Sees notation/labels, plays matching notes on MIDI | `matching`, `analytical`, `figured_bass`, `chorale` |
| **Identify** | Sees notation, labels each item by clicking | `identification`, `chorale_identification` |

---

## Play types (student plays MIDI to match what is shown)

### `matching`

The original exercise type. Student sees notes on the staff (optionally with analysis overlays — solfege, note names, Roman numerals, chord symbols, etc.) and plays the corresponding notes on the keyboard or MIDI controller.

**Grading:** `ExerciseGrader.notesMatch()` — exact MIDI pitch match.

**Use cases:** Note reading, scale/mode drills, solfege reinforcement, chord voicing practice.

**Example JSON:**
```json
{
  "type": "matching",
  "staffDistribution": "keyboard",
  "key": "jC_",
  "analysis": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": { "do_based_solfege": true, "roman_numerals": true }
  },
  "chord": [
    { "rhythmValue": "w", "visible": [65], "hidden": [] },
    { "rhythmValue": "w", "visible": [67], "hidden": [] }
  ]
}
```

---

### `analytical`

Student sees a chord with analysis annotations and plays what the analysis implies (e.g. play the chord that matches the Roman numeral shown). Graded by comparing analysis labels rather than exact pitches.

**Grading:** `ExerciseGrader.analysisMatch()` — compares derived analysis labels.

---

### `analytical_pcs`

Same as `analytical` but graded using pitch-class sets (octave-independent matching).

**Grading:** `ExerciseGrader.analysisPcsMatch()`.

---

### `figured_bass`

Student sees a bass note with figured bass notation and plays the full chord it implies.

**Grading:** `ExerciseGrader.figuredBassMatch()` — checks that the played notes realize the figures above the bass.

---

### `figured_bass_pcs`

Same as `figured_bass` but pitch-class-based (octave-independent).

**Grading:** `ExerciseGrader.figuredBassPcsMatch()`.

---

### `chorale`

Score-based play exercise using Bach chorale CIR JSON. Student plays through the score note-by-note in onset windows. Requires exactly the voices specified; handles held/tied notes.

**Grading:** `ChoraleGrader` — onset-window matching, tracks per-window statistics.

**Key files:** `chorale_grader.js`, `score_timeline.js`

**See also:** `CLAUDE.md` for full architecture and troubleshooting.

---

## Identify types (student labels notation by clicking)

### `identification`

Static chord identification. Student sees a set of notated chords on the staff. Each chord has a `?` label below it. Student clicks the label and selects the correct answer from a popup list. No MIDI input required.

**Analysis overlays are hidden** (they would give away answers).

**`identMode` variants:**

| Value | Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| `"practice"` | Correct/incorrect shown immediately after each selection |
| `"submit"` | All answers first, then Submit button reveals results |
| `"test"` | Slots lock after answering; no colour feedback shown |

**Grading:** `IdentificationGrader` — compares `answers[i]` against `problem.answer` per slot.

**Example JSON:**
```json
{
  "type": "identification",
  "identMode": "practice",
  "key": "jC_",
  "staffDistribution": "keyboard",
  "chord": [
    { "notes": [60, 64, 67], "answer": "I",  "choices": ["I", "ii", "IV", "V"] },
    { "notes": [62, 65, 69], "answer": "ii", "choices": ["I", "ii", "IV", "V"] }
  ]
}
```

**Paging:** Not yet implemented for `identification` (only `chorale_identification` has paging today), but the infrastructure in `exerciseContext` is type-agnostic and could be enabled.

---

### `chorale_identification`

Score-based identification exercise using Bach chorale CIR JSON. Student sees measures of a chorale and labels each onset window (chord position) by clicking a `?` below the staff and selecting from a popup.

**Paging:** Exercises are split into pages of 4 problems each. Students navigate with Next/Previous; a slide animation signals the page turn. Page indicator shown in the instruction text box.

**`analysisType` controls what is being identified:**

| `analysisType` | What student labels | Answer format | Example |
|----------------|-------------------|---------------|---------|
| `"roman_numeral"` | Chord function | Roman numeral | `"V7"` |
| `"figured_bass"` | Bass inversion figures | Figured bass | `"6/4"` |
| `"interval_specific"` | Interval quality + size | Quality-first | `"m3"`, `"M6"`, `"P5"` |
| `"interval_generic"` | Interval size only | Number | `"3"`, `"6"`, `"8"` |

**`compoundIntervals`** (boolean, default `false`): when `false`, intervals larger than an octave are simplified (a 10th becomes a 3rd). When `true`, compound intervals are shown as-is.

**Interval computation:** Tonal.js is the authoritative source (uses note spellings from CIR JSON, not semitone counts). `analyze.js` is used as a cross-check with `console.warn` on mismatch.

**Requires exactly 2 voices** for interval types. Enforced at import time.

**Example JSON:**
```json
{
  "type": "chorale_identification",
  "analysisType": "interval_specific",
  "compoundIntervals": false,
  "identMode": "practice",
  "score": { ... }
}
```

**Grading:** `IdentificationGrader` — same grader as `identification`, extended with `pageOffset` support so absolute answer indices work across pages.

**Key files:** `exercise_definition.js` (`computeWindowLabel`, `buildChoices`), `identification_grader.js`, `exercise_context.js` (paging state), `exercise_sheet.js` (popup, label drawing, page-turn animation).

---

## Shared infrastructure

### `IdentificationGrader`

Used by both `identification` and `chorale_identification`. Stores answers as `{ absoluteIndex: label }`. Signature:

```javascript
grade(definition, visibleProblems, pageOffset)
```

- `visibleProblems` — the current page's slice of problems (pass from `exerciseContext.getVisibleProblems()`)
- `pageOffset` — absolute index of the first visible problem (pass from `exerciseContext.getIdentPageOffset()`)

### Paging (`exerciseContext`)

Paging state lives on `exerciseContext`, not on the grader or definition:

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `getIdentPage()` | Current 0-based page number |
| `getIdentPageSize()` | Problems per page (default 4) |
| `getIdentPageOffset()` | `page * pageSize` — absolute index of first visible problem |
| `getTotalIdentPages()` | `ceil(totalProblems / pageSize)` |
| `getVisibleProblems()` | Slice of problems for current page |
| `goToIdentPage(n)` | Navigate to page n; triggers slide animation + delayed re-render |
| `submitIdentPage(options)` | Grade current page; advance if `fromUI=true` and not last page |

Currently wired only for `chorale_identification`. The same methods would work for `identification` by simply enabling them.

---

## All exercise types at a glance

| Type | Input | Grader | Paging | Notes |
|------|-------|--------|--------|-------|
| `matching` | MIDI | `ExerciseGrader.notesMatch` | No | Original app type |
| `analytical` | MIDI | `ExerciseGrader.analysisMatch` | No | |
| `analytical_pcs` | MIDI | `ExerciseGrader.analysisPcsMatch` | No | |
| `figured_bass` | MIDI | `ExerciseGrader.figuredBassMatch` | No | |
| `figured_bass_pcs` | MIDI | `ExerciseGrader.figuredBassPcsMatch` | No | |
| `chorale` | MIDI | `ChoraleGrader` | No | Score-based, onset windows |
| `identification` | Click | `IdentificationGrader` | Not yet | Static chords |
| `chorale_identification` | Click | `IdentificationGrader` | Yes (4/page) | Score-based, analysisType variants |


--------------------------------------------------
File End
--------------------------------------------------


docs/architecture.md
File type: .md
# HarmonyLab Architecture

*Written: 2026-04-09*

This document explains how HarmonyLab actually works — the mental models agents need to make correct changes.

---

## What the App Does

HarmonyLab is a music theory practice platform. Students are presented with staff notation and must either play the correct notes on a MIDI keyboard (or QWERTY keyboard / on-screen piano), or identify what they see by selecting from a multiple-choice list. The app grades each attempt in real time and records performance.

The three core objects are **Exercise**, **Playlist**, and **Course**. Courses are shown to students. Playlists are the unit of assignment. Exercises are the individual problems.

```
Course
  └── Playlists (ordered, M2M via PlaylistCourseOrdered)
        └── Exercises (ordered, M2M via ExercisePlaylistOrdered)
```

---

## Data Model

### Exercise

An `Exercise` is a single problem. Its most important field is `data` — a JSON blob that fully specifies what is notated and how it should be graded.

```json
{
  "type": "matching",
  "key": "jC_",
  "keySignature": "",
  "staffDistribution": "keyboard",
  "introText": "<p>...</p>",
  "reviewText": "",
  "analysis": {
    "enabled": true,
    "tempo": false,
    "mode": { "roman_numerals": true, "chord_labels": false, ... }
  },
  "highlight": { "enabled": false, "mode": { ... } },
  "chord": [
    { "visible": [48, 64, 67, 72], "hidden": [], "rhythmValue": "w" }
  ]
}
```

Other model fields on `Exercise`:
- `id` — human-readable slug like `EA00WI` (auto-assigned, sequential base-36)
- `description` — short optional label
- `rhythm` — space-separated rhythm string like `"w h q"` (overridden per-chord in `data.chord`)
- `time_signature` — string like `"4/4"`
- `authored_by` — the creating teacher/user
- `is_public` — whether other users can include it in their playlists
- `locked` — set to `True` after any student has performed it (prevents editing)
- `tags` — array of strings

**The `chord` array is the exercise content.** Each entry is one chord the student must play, in order. `visible` = notes shown on staff; `hidden` = notes student must supply; `rhythmValue` = duration (`w` whole, `h` half, `q` quarter).

### Exercise Types

The `type` field determines the grading logic:

| Type | `visible` | `hidden` | What student does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matching` | all notes | `[]` | Play what you see |
| `analytical` | `[]` | all notes | Notes hidden; roman numeral overlay shown — identify by ear |
| `figured_bass` | bass note only | upper voices | Bass shown; student fills in upper voices from figures |
| `identification` | all notes | `[]` | See notes, pick the answer from a multiple-choice list |
| `chorale` | (see below) | — | Play a Bach chorale segment, onset by onset |

For `identification`, each chord dict also has `"answer"` and `"choices"` keys.

For `chorale`, the `data` dict contains a `"score"` key with a CIR (Canonical Internal Representation) JSON object instead of a `"chord"` array. See `claude.md` and `docs/chorale_exercises_plan.md` for the full chorale system.

### Key Format

Keys are encoded as a 4-character string: `jC_` = C major, `iA_` = A minor.

- First char: `j` = major, `i` = minor
- Next chars: note name with accidental (`C`, `G`, `F#`, `Bb`, `Eb`, etc.)
- Trailing `_` = natural (no accidental in the name)

Full mapping:
```
jC_ jG_ jD_ jA_ jE_ jB_ jF# jDb jAb jEb jBb jF_
iA_ iE_ iB_ iF# iC# iG# iD_ iG_ iC_ iF_ iBb iEb
```

The key affects note spelling via `keyMap` in `lab/static/js/src/config/general.js` — enharmonic spelling (e.g. F# vs Gb) depends on the key. **MIDI note numbers are absolute pitch-class; the `key` field controls how they are spelled on the staff.** This is why being in the wrong key causes notes to appear with wrong accidentals (G## instead of A).

### Staff Distribution

`staffDistribution` controls the staff layout:

| Value | Layout |
|---|---|
| `keyboard` | Grand staff (treble + bass), standard keyboard split |
| `keyboardPlusLHBias` | Grand staff, bass dominant (e.g. ROTO exercises) |
| `keyboardPlusRHBias` | Grand staff, treble dominant |
| `RH` | Treble staff only |
| `LH` | Bass staff only |
| `grandStaff` | Grand staff, no keyboard |
| `chorale` | SATB chorale layout (S+A treble, T+B bass) |

### Playlist

A `Playlist` is an ordered sequence of exercises. Key fields:
- `exercises` — M2M to `Exercise` via `ExercisePlaylistOrdered` (has an `order` field)
- `transpose_requests` — list of key signature strings (e.g. `["C", "G", "D"]`)
- `transposition_type` — `"Exercise Loop"` or `"Playlist Loop"` (or null = no transposition)
- `is_auto` — True if auto-generated when exercises were saved (not manually curated)

**Transposition** is the primary mechanism for presenting the same exercise in multiple keys without duplicating Exercise objects. If a playlist has 3 exercises and `transpose_requests: ["C", "G", "D"]` with `transposition_type: "Exercise Loop"`, the playlist virtually expands to 9 exercises: A+C, A+G, A+D, B+C, B+G, B+D, C+C, C+G, C+D. Transposed exercises get dynamically generated IDs like `EA00DD+16`.

### Course

A `Course` is an ordered collection of playlists assigned to students. Key fields:
- `playlists` — M2M to `Playlist` via `PlaylistCourseOrdered`
- `open` — if True, visible to all the teacher's student connections; if False, only to specified groups
- `timely_credit / tardy_credit / late_credit / tardy_threshold` — due-date grading weights
- `authored_by` — the teacher who owns the course

---

## How Exercises Are Served (Request Flow)

```
Student hits URL
  ↓
Django view (lab/views.py: PlaylistView / ExerciseView / CourseView)
  ↓
generate_exercise_context() assembles:
  - exercise.data (all the music content)
  - navigation: nextExercise, previousExercise, exerciseList
  - playlistName, courseId, exerciseNum
  - exerciseIsPerformed, exerciseErrorCount (from PerformanceData)
  ↓
RequirejsContext.set_module_params("app/components/app/exercise", context)
  ↓
Django renders exercise.html template
  ↓
Browser loads RequireJS → main.js → app/components/app/exercise AMD module
  ↓
JS reads exercise data via module.config() (injected by Django as requirejs.config JSON)
  ↓
ExerciseDefinition parses data → ExerciseContext manages state
  ↓
ExerciseSheetComponent renders VexFlow notation on <canvas id="staff">
  ↓
MIDI/keyboard input → grader (ExerciseGrader / ChoraleGrader / IdentificationGrader)
  ↓
Performance data POSTed to submit_exercise_performance view → PerformanceData saved
```

The JS app never makes its own Django API calls to load exercise data — everything is injected into the page as inline JSON at render time via `module.config()`.

---

## Frontend Architecture

The frontend uses RequireJS (AMD modules). There is no bundler in dev mode — each module loads individually. An optional build at `data/requirejs/build.json` can point to a compiled bundle.

**Boot sequence:**
1. Django injects `requirejs.config(...)` into the page (paths, shims, module params)
2. `main.js` reads `module.config().app_module` and requires it
3. The app module (e.g. `app/components/app/exercise`) wires together components

**Key JS files:**
- `lab/static/js/src/main.js` — RequireJS bootstrap
- `lab/static/js/src/components/app/exercise.js` — exercise app (wires piano + sheet + grader)
- `lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_definition.js` — parses exercise data JSON
- `lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_context.js` — manages state (current chord, score)
- `lab/static/js/src/components/music/exercise_sheet.js` — renders VexFlow canvas
- `lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_grader.js` — grading for matching/analytical/figured_bass
- `lab/static/js/src/models/chorale_grader.js` — grading for chorales
- `lab/static/js/src/models/identification_grader.js` — grading for identification

**Adding a new AMD module:** add a `paths` entry in `harmony/settings/requirejs.py`. Never move files without updating that file.

---

## Grading

### Standard Exercises (matching / analytical / figured_bass)

`ExerciseGrader` compares the set of MIDI notes currently held against the expected chord's `visible + hidden` notes. The student advances to the next chord when all expected notes are held simultaneously.

### Identification Exercises

`IdentificationGrader` waits for the student to click a multiple-choice answer button rather than playing notes. The `answer` and `choices` fields on each chord dict drive the UI.

### Chorale Exercises

`ChoraleGrader` uses an onset-based window system — the score is parsed into time-ordered groups of notes, and the student must play each group in sequence. See `claude.md` for the full algorithm.

---

## Performance Data

`PerformanceData` records are keyed to `(user, playlist, course)`. Each record has a `data` JSON array — one entry per exercise attempted, with `id`, `error_tally`, `tempo_rating`, and other metrics. The gradebook views in `apps/exercises/views.py` and the dashboard read from these records.

---

## Non-Obvious Patterns

**Exercise keys are baked in.** An Exercise object has a specific `key` in its `data`. The key controls both note spelling on the staff and the analytical overlay (Roman numerals, figured bass). You cannot display the same Exercise in a different key without either transposing it or generating a new Exercise.

**Multi-key content via playlist transposition.** One Exercise can be presented in multiple keys by adding `transpose_requests` to the playlist. Transposed copies get virtual IDs and are generated on the fly — no duplicate Exercise rows.

**Auto-playlists.** Every time a teacher creates an exercise through the editor, `Exercise.set_auto_playlist()` adds it to an auto-generated playlist (`is_auto=True`). This is a convenience feature so newly-created exercises are immediately playable. Auto-playlists are created per session (within the last 8 hours).

**`locked` prevents editing.** Once `PerformanceData` exists for an exercise, it is locked. This prevents teachers from changing an exercise that students have already answered (which would invalidate their scores).

**RequireJS paths are the source of truth for the frontend.** If a JS file moves, update `harmony/settings/requirejs.py` or the module will 404 silently.

**`keySignature` vs `key`.** `key` is the HarmonyLab key string (`jC_`). `keySignature` is the staff key signature string used by VexFlow (empty string for C major, `"F"` for one flat, etc.). Both are typically set; `keySignature` can be derived from `key` but they are stored separately.


--------------------------------------------------
File End
--------------------------------------------------


docs/hosting_and_roadmap.md
File type: .md
# HarmonyLab: Hosting, Modernization & Product Roadmap

*Written: 2026-04-02*

---

## Background

HarmonyLab has been hosted on Heroku by a collaborator. With that collaboration becoming unreliable, self-hosting is the logical next step. This document covers:

1. Hosting options and migration plan
2. What deployment actually requires
3. LMS assessment and modernization strategy
4. Product direction: mouse/keyboard input, course library, monetization

---

## 1. Hosting: Fly.io vs Heroku

### Cost Comparison

| Factor | Heroku | Fly.io |
|---|---|---|
| Free tier | None (removed 2022) | Yes (shared CPU, 256MB RAM) |
| Cheapest paid compute | ~$7/mo (Eco dyno) | ~$2–5/mo |
| Postgres | $5–9/mo (mini) | $3/mo (1GB shared) |
| Static files | WhiteNoise works | WhiteNoise works |
| SSL | Included | Included |
| Deployment method | Git push + Procfile | Needs Dockerfile |
| Django support | Mature, documented | Well-supported |
| **Estimated total** | **~$12–16/mo** | **~$5–8/mo** |

### Recommendation

**Fly.io is the better long-term choice** — roughly half the cost, more control, and no vendor lock-in. The tradeoff is a one-time setup cost: writing a Dockerfile and `fly.toml` config (each ~40 lines).

**If speed matters most right now**, Heroku is the path of least resistance. The existing `Procfile` and `harmony/settings/heroku.py` mean deploying to a new Heroku account is a few commands.

---

## 2. What Deployment Requires

### Current State

The app is already Heroku-ready:
- `Procfile` runs migrations, creates the cache table, and starts gunicorn:
  ```
  release: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py createcachetable
  web: gunicorn harmony.wsgi:application --log-file -
  ```
- `harmony/settings/heroku.py` handles production config
- WhiteNoise serves static files (no S3/CDN needed)
- Sentry integration for error tracking

### Heroku (Fastest Path)

1. Create new Heroku app + Postgres addon
2. Set environment variables:
   - `SECRET_KEY`
   - `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=harmony.settings.heroku`
   - `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (JSON list of your domain)
   - `EMAIL_HOST_USER` / `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD` (Gmail SMTP for password reset)
   - `SENTRY_DSN` (optional)
3. `git push heroku master` — migrations run automatically

### Fly.io (Cheaper Path)

Same env vars, plus:
1. Write a `Dockerfile` (Python 3.10, install Pipfile deps, run gunicorn)
2. Write `fly.toml` (app name, region, port, health check)
   - Use the `[deploy] release_command` field to run migrations and `createcachetable` — this is the Fly.io equivalent of Heroku's `release` dyno
3. Create Fly Postgres cluster: `fly postgres create`
4. `fly deploy`

### One-Time Tasks Either Way

- Transfer the PostgreSQL database from the old host (pg_dump / pg_restore)
- Update DNS to point your domain at the new host
- Verify email sending works (password reset flow)
- Test MIDI input in Chrome/Edge after deploy

---

## 3. LMS Assessment

### What the App Is

HarmonyLab is not a traditional LMS — it is a **music theory practice platform with instructor features**. The exercise engine (MIDI grading, VexFlow notation, chorale analysis) is genuinely sophisticated and is the core differentiator. No off-the-shelf LMS (Moodle, Canvas, Open edX) does what this does.

### What Feels Dated

| Area | Current State | Modern Standard |
|---|---|---|
| Module system | RequireJS (2013) | ES modules / Vite |
| Frontend interaction | jQuery + full page reloads | React/Vue SPA or htmx |
| CSS framework | Bootstrap 4 (EOL) | Bootstrap 5 or Tailwind |
| Django version | 2.2 (EOL, no security updates) | 5.2 LTS (supported until April 2028) |
| Auth options | Email/password only | + Google/SSO |
| Student dashboard | None | Progress, completion, streaks |
| Mobile support | None (WebMIDI is desktop-only) | Responsive UI at minimum |
| Teacher UI | Admin panel only | Purpose-built course builder |

### Modernization Options

**Option A: Incremental improvement (recommended)**
- Upgrade Django to 5.2 LTS (current LTS, supported until April 2028) — critical for security
- Replace RequireJS with Vite — big developer experience improvement
- Add a modern student dashboard (progress bars, completion rates, history)
- Add htmx for partial-page updates without a full SPA rewrite
- Keep the Django backend — correct choice for this domain

**Option B: Frontend rewrite with React or Vue**
- Replace Django templates with a React SPA
- Django becomes a REST API (Django REST Framework)
- Much larger effort (months, not weeks)
- The music engine (VexFlow, Tone.js, graders) would carry over unchanged
- Enables mobile and richer interactivity long-term

**Option C: Adopt an existing LMS**
- Not viable. Canvas/Moodle/Open edX don't support custom MIDI exercises.
- The exercise engine is the entire product.

### Recommendation

Start with **Option A**. The Django upgrade alone (2.2 → 5.2) removes a meaningful security risk and unlocks modern Django features. Then layer in UX improvements. Reserve a full SPA rewrite for a later phase when the course library and user base justify it.

**Note on the Django upgrade:** The jump from 2.2 to 5.2 spans three major versions and will require updating several pinned dependencies that have had breaking changes:

| Package | Pinned version | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `whitenoise` | 5.1.0 | Known issues with Django 4+; upgrade to 6.x |
| `dj-database-url` | 0.5.0 | API changed significantly in 1.x |
| `psycopg2-binary` | 2.8.6 | Update to 2.9.x |
| `pytz` | 2020.1 | Superseded by Python 3.9+ built-in `zoneinfo` |
| `chardet` | 3.0.4 | Very old; may have transitive conflicts |

Factor this dependency chain into the effort estimate — the actual upgrade is closer to **1–2 weeks** than a few days. Python 3.10 security support also ends October 2026, so a Python upgrade (3.10 → 3.12) is worth bundling with the Django upgrade.

---

## 4. Product Direction

### Mouse & Keyboard Input

The exercises currently accept MIDI keyboard input. Gaps to fill for non-MIDI users:

- **Clickable staff notation** — click a note head in the score to "play" it
- **On-screen piano keyboard** — click keys with a mouse
- **Computer keyboard note entry** — letter keys for pitch (A–G), numbers for octave, like Sibelius/Finale
- **All three are buildable** on top of VexFlow + the existing grader infrastructure without rearchitecting

This is the highest-leverage near-term feature — it removes the MIDI hardware requirement and opens the app to all students, not just those with MIDI controllers.

### Built-in Exercise Library (The Real Artusi Advantage)

Artusi's actual competitive strength is not its exercise engine — it's that students open it and there is already a full semester of structured work ready to go. Teachers don't have to build anything; they assign from a library.

HarmonyLab currently has no built-in library. All content is user-created. A teacher starting fresh has to build every exercise, playlist, and course themselves.

**This is the most important content gap to close before the pilot.**

#### What the library needs to contain

A standard undergraduate theory sequence (2 semesters) would cover:

| Unit | Exercise Types | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Intervals | Identify and notate intervals | All qualities, all sizes |
| Scales & modes | Identify and complete scales | Major, minor, modal |
| Triads | Build and identify triads | All qualities, root position + inversions |
| Seventh chords | Build and identify 7ths | All types |
| Voice leading basics | 4-part SATB writing | Already strong (chorale grader) |
| Roman numeral analysis | Identify chords in context | Already exists |
| Secondary dominants | Tonicization | Extension of existing analysis |
| Species counterpoint | 1st–4th species | Not yet implemented |
| Harmonic dictation | Hear → identify progression | Not yet implemented |
| Melodic dictation | Hear → notate melody | Not yet implemented |

The top half of this table (intervals through Roman numerals) is buildable now using existing exercise types. The bottom half requires new exercise type development.

**The author's advantage:** Building this library is a content task, not an engineering task. A music theory teacher can create dozens of exercises per hour once the workflow is smooth. The priority is making that creation workflow fast and then populating the library.

#### How the library should be structured

**For teachers:**
- A dedicated **Content Library** page — browse all public courses, playlists, and exercises
- Filter by topic (intervals, triads, voice leading…), difficulty, exercise type
- One-click "Copy to my courses" — clone a public course and customize it
- This is the model Artusi uses: teachers adopt and adapt, not build from scratch

**For students:**
- A dedicated **My Work** page (replaces the current confusing "Courses By Other Users")
  - Shows only courses the student is enrolled in via their groups
  - Clear completion status per playlist
  - Due dates visible if set
- A **Free Practice** section — browse public exercises/playlists not tied to a course
  - Good for self-study, exam prep, exploration

#### Current browsing UX (and its problems)

The current system is connection/permission-based, not enrollment-based:

1. Teacher creates a Group → adds students manually by email → creates a Course → assigns Course to Group
2. Student sees it under "Courses By Other Users" — a flat list of all courses from anyone who's granted them content access, enrolled or not
3. There is **no public library page** — `is_public` content is accessible but not browsable
4. There is **no "My Assigned Work" view** — students can't distinguish "this was assigned to me" from "I can access this"
5. To find a teacher's course, a student must first manually add the teacher as a connection

This friction is acceptable in the current small-scale use but won't work for a class of 30 students who have never used the app.

#### What needs to be built

| Feature | What it does | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **Public library page** | Browse all `is_public` courses/playlists/exercises, filter by topic | 2–3 days |
| **"My Work" student view** | Shows only courses assigned via groups; replaces "Courses By Others" | 2–3 days |
| **Copy/clone a public course** | Teacher clones a library course and customizes it | 1–2 days |
| **Join code enrollment** | Student enters code → added to teacher's group automatically (replaces manual email add) | 1–2 days |
| **Content tagging** | Tag exercises/playlists by topic (intervals, voice leading, etc.) for filtering | 1–2 days |

#### Artusi feature gap

| Feature | HarmonyLab Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Chorale voice leading | Done (advanced) | None |
| Chord identification & Roman numerals | Done | None |
| Interval exercises | Exists | Library content needed |
| Triad/seventh chord exercises | Exists | Library content needed |
| Species counterpoint | Not implemented | New exercise type |
| Harmonic dictation | Not implemented | New exercise type |
| Melodic dictation | Not implemented | New exercise type |
| Public browsable library | Not implemented | Build browse UI |
| Student "My Work" dashboard | Not implemented | Build view |
| Teacher gradebook | Partial (course_activity view exists) | Polish UI |
| Payment / subscriptions | Not implemented | Phase 3 |

### User Roles: Teacher vs Student

The original design deliberately avoided separate teacher/student account types — all users share one model, keeping things fluid. This was a reasonable choice and the role distinction is already implicit in the data:

- A user who is `Group.manager` → is acting as a teacher
- A user who is a `Group.member` → is acting as a student
- `content_permits` / `performance_permits` → teacher grants student access

**Recommendation: don't add a separate model or role flag yet.** Use `Group.manager` as the teacher signal. If billing is added later, a single `role` field (`teacher` / `student`, set at registration) is the clean Django way — one field with `TextChoices`, not two booleans. Avoid `is_teacher + is_student` booleans (anti-pattern: what does both=True mean?).

### Monetization Model

The model mirrors Artusi's: **anyone can use the app for free; the paywall is around the classroom relationship**, not content access.

- Free tier: practice exercises, create playlists/courses, self-study
- Paid tier: joining a teacher's class, teacher seeing student performance data

This is clean because the billing attaches to the `Group` — the object that represents the classroom relationship. A `stripe_subscription_id` on `Group` (or a FK to a `Subscription` model) is all that's needed structurally. Exercise/Playlist/Course models don't need to change.

**Business model options:**
- **Per-student subscription** (~$15–25/semester) — matches Artusi pricing
- **Per-institution license** — flat fee for unlimited students at a school
- **Freemium** — free tier real and useful, paid tier for classroom features

**Teacher verification:** Require `.edu` email for teacher accounts at registration — one line of validation, matches how Artusi handles it. Not airtight but sufficient at early scale.

**Ongoing support costs** (realistic expectations):
- Disputed charges / forgotten subscriptions — small but real
- Non-.edu teacher requests (adjuncts, private teachers, international) — need a manual approval path
- Mid-semester cancellations — need a policy decision (lose access immediately? end of semester?)
- Institution deals — once you have traction, schools want one invoice for 30 students

None of these are engineering problems. The engineering is a one-time ~2-week effort; the support is operational.

**Implementation effort when ready:**
| Piece | Effort |
|---|---|
| Add `role` field + registration UI update | 1 day |
| Email verification before account activation | 1–2 days |
| `.edu` check for teacher registration | 2 hours |
| Stripe Checkout (one-time or subscription) | 2–3 days |
| Access control on Group join/view | 1 day |
| Subscription management page (cancel, update card) | 1–2 days |
| **Total** | **~2 weeks** |

### College Pilot (Before Monetizing)

The right sequence is: **pilot at your college first, charge later.** Running real students through the app will reveal what actually matters before building billing infrastructure.

#### What the data model already supports for a classroom

Inspecting the actual models, more is built than expected:

```
Group (manager=teacher, members=students)
  └── Course (visible_to → Groups)
        └── Playlist (ordered, with due dates commented out but schema present)
              └── Exercise

PerformanceData (user + playlist + course → every attempt recorded)
Course already has: timely_credit, tardy_credit, late_credit, tardy_threshold fields
```

The classroom relationship, grading weights, and per-student performance data are all modeled. What's missing is the **UI to use them**.

#### What needs to be built for the pilot

| Feature | What | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **Join codes** | Teacher creates Group → gets a code (e.g. `MUSIC201-F26`); student enters code → auto-enrolled. Requires one `join_code` field on `Group` + one view. | 1–2 days |
| **Student dashboard** | "My courses, assignments, completion, scores" — the data is in `PerformanceData`, just needs a view and template | 3–5 days |
| **Teacher gradebook** | Class roster + completion/score per playlist per student — again, data exists, needs a view | 3–5 days |
| **Due date UI** | `Course` already has `timely_credit`, `tardy_credit`, `late_credit`, `tardy_threshold` fields. The UI for setting due dates per playlist is the missing piece. | 2–3 days |

**Total for a usable college pilot: ~2–3 weeks.** No structural changes to Exercise/Playlist/Course needed.

docs/grading_pipeline.md
File type: .md
# Grading and Follow‑Along Pipeline

This note documents the original (legacy) grading flow and how the new chorale/CIR path integrates with it.

## Legacy pipeline (single‑chord problems)
- Capture: MIDI events update the `ExerciseChordBank` (inputChords).
- Grading trigger: `ExerciseContext` listens to `inputChords.change` and calls `grade()`.
- Grader: `ExerciseGrader.grade(definition, inputChords)` compares each chord against `definition.getProblems()` and returns:
  - `result`: `correct | partial | incorrect`
  - `activeIndex`: next expected chord index (advances when matched)
  - `problems[]`: per‑chord match info
- State machine in `ExerciseContext.grade()`:
  - Updates `this.state`: `READY → WAITING → CORRECT | FINISHED | INCORRECT`
  - Starts timer on first input; calls `endTimer()` when complete; compiles and `submitExerciseReport()` once
  - Broadcasts `EVENTS.BROADCAST.NEXT_CHORD` when `activeIndex` advances
  - Auto navigation:
    - If flawless: `triggerNextExercise()` (gated by `general.autoAdvance`)
    - If mistakes: `triggerRepeatExercise()` or `triggerNextExercise()` depending on `general.ignoreMistakesOnAutoAdvance`

## Chorale/CIR pipeline (polyphonic follow‑along)
- Timeline: `ScoreTimeline.buildTimeline(score, { maxMeasures })` flattens the CIR score into onset windows, with monotonically increasing `onset` ticks.
- Renderer: `VexflowAdapter.render(score, { playedNoteIds, ... })` draws the first N measures and highlights noteheads whose timeline `id` is in `playedNoteIds`.
- Follow‑along and grading (implemented in `components/music/exercise_sheet.js`):
  - NOTE ON:
    - Start timer on first note if not running
    - Within current onset window (at pointer), match MIDI to unplayed notes; mark `playedNoteIds`
    - If all timeline events are played within the visible range, set `ExerciseContext.state` to `CORRECT` (no mistakes) or `FINISHED` (mistakes); call `endTimer()` and `submitExerciseReport()` once; then auto‑advance or repeat via `triggerNextExercise()` / `triggerRepeatExercise()` (gated by config)
  - NOTE OFF:
    - When all notes for the current onset are played and released, advance the timeline pointer to the first event of the next onset
    - Broadcast `EVENTS.BROADCAST.NEXT_CHORD` to notify listeners of progression

## Config flags used
- `general.autoAdvance` / `general.autoAdvanceDelay`
- `general.autoRepeat` / `general.autoRepeatDelay`
- `general.ignoreMistakesOnAutoAdvance`

## Integration guarantees
- Same ExerciseContext state transitions (`READY/WAITING/FINISHED/CORRECT`)
- Same next‑chord broadcast on progression
- Same auto‑advance and auto‑repeat triggers and gating
- Timer is recorded (duration always; tempo metrics appear when supported)

## Next steps (optional)
- Add per‑window timepoints to support tempo metrics similar to legacy grading.
- Visual cursor for the active onset window, synchronized with the pointer.
- Expand maxMeasures windowing to a moving viewport with smooth scroll.

## Pending Features (High Priority)

### Feature 2: Visual Feedback for Incorrect Notes

**Objective:** Color incorrect notes red in the VexFlow renderer for immediate visual feedback.

**Current State:**
- Notes are colored gray (unplayed) or black (played correctly)
- No visual distinction for incorrect notes
- Students don't know which wrong notes they played

**Implementation:**

**File:** `lab/static/js/src/components/music/rendering/vexflow_adapter.js` (lines 371-411)

**Step 1: Create incorrectNoteIds Set in chorale_grader.js**

In `reset()`:
```javascript
this.incorrectNoteIds = new Set();  // Track IDs of notes that were played incorrectly
```

In `noteOn()` when a wrong note is detected (line 254):
```javascript
// NEW: Track the incorrect note ID for visual feedback
// (We need to add ID tracking when wrong notes are played)
```

**Step 2: Expose incorrectNoteIds to the renderer**

In `exercise_context.js`, pass incorrectNoteIds to VexFlow adapter:
```javascript
var idState = {
  playedNoteIds: this.grader.playedNoteIds,
  incorrectNoteIds: this.grader.incorrectNoteIds,  // NEW
  nextId: nextId
};
```

**Step 3: Update VexFlow coloring logic**

In `vexflow_adapter.js`:
```javascript
var noteId = idState.nextId || 0;
var played = idState.playedNoteIds && idState.playedNoteIds.has(noteId);
var incorrect = idState.incorrectNoteIds && idState.incorrectNoteIds.has(noteId);

if (incorrect) {
  note.setStyle({ fillStyle: '#FF0000', strokeStyle: '#FF0000' });  // Red
} else if (played) {
  note.setStyle({ fillStyle: '#000000', strokeStyle: '#000000' });  // Black
} else {
  note.setStyle({ fillStyle: '#9aa0a6', strokeStyle: '#9aa0a6' });  // Gray
}
```

**Challenge:** We need to track which timeline event IDs correspond to incorrect notes. Currently, when a wrong note is played, we don't have the timeline event ID - we only have the MIDI pitch. We need to either:
1. Store event IDs when wrong notes are detected, OR
2. Find the wrong note in the timeline after the fact

**Testing:**
1. Load a chorale exercise
2. Play a wrong note
3. Verify the note appears in red in the score
4. Play a correct note - verify it turns black
5. Verify unplayed notes remain gray

## Pending Features (Medium Priority)

### Feature 4: Mode Variations

**Objective:** Support different playing modes (play outer voices only, soprano only, with figured bass, etc.)

**Current State:**
- All exercises use "play-all-voices" mode
- No mode variations in exercise definition
- No voice filtering in grader

**Available Modes:**
1. `play-all-voices` - All four SATB voices (current)
2. `play-outer` - Soprano + Bass only (for bass line practice)
3. `play-soprano` - Soprano only (melody only)
4. `play-bass-figures` - Bass with figured bass symbols
5. `play-inner` - Alto + Tenor only (inner voice practice)

**Implementation:**

**File:** `lab/static/js/src/models/chorale_grader.js`

**Step 1: Filter timeline by mode in initFromDefinition()**

After building timeline (line 55):
```javascript
// Filter timeline based on mode
var mode = definition.data.mode || 'play-all-voices';
if (mode !== 'play-all-voices') {
  this.timeline = this._filterTimelineByMode(this.timeline, mode);
}
```

**Step 2: Implement _filterTimelineByMode()**

```javascript
_filterTimelineByMode: function (timeline, mode) {
  var voiceFilter = {
    'play-soprano': ['treble-0'],     // Voice 0 = soprano
    'play-bass': ['bass-0'],          // Bass staff, voice 0
    'play-outer': ['treble-0', 'bass-0'],
    'play-inner': ['treble-1', 'bass-1'],  // Voice 1 = alto/tenor
  };

  if (!voiceFilter[mode]) return timeline;

  var allowedVoices = voiceFilter[mode];
  return timeline.filter(function(ev) {
    var voiceKey = ev.staff + '-' + ev.voiceIndex;
    return allowedVoices.indexOf(voiceKey) !== -1;
  });
},
```

**Step 3: Update exercise definition**

In `import_chorale.py` (line 68):
```python
"mode": "play-all-voices",  # Can be: play-all-voices, play-outer, play-soprano, etc.
```

**Testing:**
1. Import exercise with mode="play-soprano"
2. Verify only soprano notes are expected
3. Verify bass/alto notes are grayed out or hidden
4. Verify playing bass notes is marked INCORRECT

### Feature 5: Grading Configuration

**Objective:** Make grading configuration actually functional (currently ignored).

**Current State:**
- Grading config exists in exercise definition (lines 80-84 of import_chorale.py)
- Config is never used - all values ignored
- Hard-coded behavior only

```python
"grading": {
    "onsetWindowMs": 150,           # Unused
    "releaseTolerancePct": 40,      # Unused
    "octaveFlexible": False         # Unused
}
```

**Implementation:**

**Step 1: Implement releaseTolerancePct**

Currently: Notes must be held until next window starts
Desired: Release can happen up to N% after window end

In `chorale_grader.js` noteOff():
```javascript
noteOff: function (midi) {
  var config = this._config;  // Store grading config in grader
  var toleranceMs = (config.releaseTolerancePct / 100) * 1024;  // ticks

  // Allow late release if within tolerance
  if (this.heldMidi.has(midi)) {
    this.heldMidi.delete(midi);
  }
},
```

**Step 2: Implement octaveFlexible**

Currently: C4 (MIDI 60) matches only C4
Desired: If true, any octave's C matches

In `noteOn()` matching logic:
```javascript
var config = this._config;
var midi_matches = function(played, expected) {
  if (played === expected) return true;
  if (config.octaveFlexible) {
    return (played % 12) === (expected % 12);  // Same note, any octave
  }
  return false;
};
```

**Step 3: Make onsetWindowMs functional**

Currently: Windows are fixed at exact onsets
Desired: Allow notes within ±onsetWindowMs to match

Currently hardcoded merge: 1024 ticks (1 beat)
Could be configurable: `config.onsetWindowMs * (4096 / 60000 / tempo)`

**Testing:**
1. Create exercise with octaveFlexible: true
2. Play a note in different octave - should match
3. Create exercise with octaveFlexible: false
4. Play same note in different octave - should be INCORRECT
5. Test releaseTolerancePct with held notes

## Technical Debt & Cleanup

### Issue 1: Configuration Storage in Grader

Currently, the grader receives config in `initFromDefinition()` but doesn't store it.

**Solution:** Store config object:
```javascript
initFromDefinition: function (definition) {
  this._config = definition.data.grading || {};  // Store for later use
  // ...
}
```

### Issue 2: Timeline Event IDs for Incorrect Notes

When tracking incorrect notes, we need timeline event IDs for rendering feedback.

**Current:** incorrectNotes = { windowIndex: [midi1, midi2] }
**Needed:** Ability to map MIDI pitch back to event IDs

**Solution:** When wrong note detected, find matching timeline events:
```javascript
if (!matched) {
  // Find and store event IDs of unplayed notes with this MIDI
  var wrongEventIds = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < currentWindow.length; i++) {
    if (tl[currentWindow[i]].midi === midi && !this.playedNoteIds.has(tl[currentWindow[i]].id)) {
      wrongEventIds.push(tl[currentWindow[i]].id);
    }
  }
  this.incorrectNoteIds.add(...wrongEventIds);
}
```

### Issue 3: Exercise Definition Validation

No validation of mode/grading config values.

**Solution:** Add validation in exercise_definition.js:
```javascript
isValidMode: function() {
  var valid = ['play-all-voices', 'play-outer', 'play-soprano'];
  return valid.indexOf(this.data.mode) !== -1;
}
```

# HarmonyLab Documentation

This directory contains comprehensive documentation for the HarmonyLab system, including implementation guides, roadmaps, and assessments.

## Exercise Type Reference

docs/chorale_exercises_plan.md
File type: .md
# Chorale Exercises Plan

This document captures a practical plan to turn the imported Bach chorales into interactive Exercises that students perform on a MIDI keyboard with real‑time correctness feedback and stored grades, while keeping Play mode for exploration and demos.

## Goals
- Reuse existing Play flow for preview and analysis selection.
- Generate Exercises from whole pieces or excerpts with minimal friction.
- Provide immediate note‑level feedback (gray → black when correct), and persist grades.
- Scaffold a lightweight curriculum that we can grow incrementally.

## Exercise Templates (auto‑generatable per chorale/excerpt)
Each template defines what’s displayed, what students must perform, and how grading works. All reuse the same runtime: timeline → expected notes → MIDI matcher → coloring + grade.

1) Play the outer voices (Soprano + Bass)
- Display: Soprano and Bass notation. Optional: faint inner voices.
- Task: Perform S & B in time.
- Grading: pitch exact (or octave‑flex toggled), onset window (e.g., ±120 ms), release tolerance (≥40% of notated duration). Per‑measure aggregation.

2) Play the soprano (melody)
- Display: Soprano line; metronome / bar cursor.
- Task: Perform melody.
- Grading: per‑note accuracy; bonus for mistake‑free phrases.

3) Play the bass with figures
- Display: Bass staff + figured‑bass (or Roman numerals).
- Task: v1: perform bass only; v2 (advanced): add chord members at onsets.
- Grading: v1 = bass only; v2 = require ≥k correct chord tones at each onset.

4) Fill inner voices
- Display: Outer voices + figures; inner voices are placeholders.
- Task: Perform missing inner notes at each onset.
- Grading: chord‑membership matching; enharmonic‑robust; no parallel checks in v1.

5) Cadence micro‑drills
- Display: 1–2 measures around a cadence.
- Task: Perform those bars.
- Grading: compact rubric per cadence; optional “first‑pass” bonus.

## Data shape (Exercise.data)
Add the following fields (non‑breaking; defaults preserve current behavior):

- mode: "play-outer" | "play-soprano" | "play-bass-figures" | "fill-inner" | "cadence-drill"
- targetVoices: ["soprano","bass"] or staff/voice indices (e.g., { treble:[0], bass:[1] })
- display: { showFigures: bool, showRomans: bool, transpose: int, tempo: int, waitMode: bool }
- grading: { onsetWindowMs: int, releaseTolerancePct: number, octaveFlexible: bool, chordMemberMin: int }
- excerpt: { startMeasure: int, endMeasure: int }
- score: existing CIR JSON
- events: optional precomputed onset/hold timeline (derive if missing)

## Runtime feedback (VF adapter + MIDI)
- Rendering: notes draw gray initially; a correctness map keyed by (measure, staff, voice, noteIdx) toggles style to black when satisfied; brief red flash on wrong.
- Transport: either fixed tempo or waitMode that advances only when current onset is satisfied.
- Matching (per onset):
  1. Collect expected pitches for target voices at time t.
  2. Accept student note if within onsetWindowMs and matches pitch (or pitch class if octaveFlexible).
  3. Mark satisfied; require all expected notes for stacked chords.
  4. Hold check: consider satisfied if held ≥ releaseTolerancePct of notated duration.

## Importer & generation
- Management command: ingest `data/corpus/bach/*.json` into `Exercise` rows.
  - Title = BWV + incipit; tags = { composer:Bach, corpus:Chorale, key, meter, pickup }.
  - Generate 2–3 templates per chorale with short excerpts (e.g., measures 1–4, 5–8).
  - Preserve existing workflow: you can still create from Play and "Save as Exercise"; this command is an optional batch path.

## Curriculum skeleton
- Unit 1: Melody & Cadences — play‑soprano, cadence micro‑drills.
- Unit 2: Bass & Figures — play‑bass‑figures simple → with 7ths/suspensions.
- Unit 3: Outer Voices Together — play‑outer slow → normal tempo.
- Unit 4: Inner Voices — fill‑inner 2–4 measure excerpts.
- Unit 5: Modulation (later) — pivot/secondary dominants.

## Integration with current save‑from‑Play flow
- In Play, after choosing analysis/figures, "Save as Exercise" populates Exercise.data with:
  - mode based on current view (e.g., soprano‑only / outer voices).
  - targetVoices from UI selection (e.g., &voices=sb).
  - display flags for figures/romans; tempo; transpose.
  - excerpt bounds if you set a measure range.
- The existing Dashboard listing picks up the new Exercise; you can still attach simple rhythms as today (polyphony optional later).

## Acceptance criteria
- Students get per‑note immediate feedback and a stored grade for each generated Exercise.
- First iteration supports at least modes: play‑soprano, play‑outer, cadence‑drill.
- Existing Play → Save path still works and produces Exercises that render in the Dashboard.

## Next steps
1. Implement correctness coloring hook in VexFlow adapter.
2. Add simple MIDI matcher with onset/hold windows.
3. Seed 6–10 Exercises from the five chorales and attach them to three starter Units.
4. Add optional batch importer command for bulk generation.

docs/identification_exercise.md
File type: .md
# Identification Exercise Type

An identification exercise shows the student a set of notated chords and asks them to label each one by clicking a question-mark placeholder below the staff and selecting from a list of choices. No MIDI input is used.

---

## JSON Data Format

```json
{
  "type": "identification",
  "identMode": "submit",
  "key": "jC_",
  "staffDistribution": "keyboard",
  "chord": [
    {
      "notes": [60, 64, 67],
      "answer": "I",
      "choices": ["I", "ii", "IV", "V"]
    },
    {
      "notes": [62, 65, 69],
      "answer": "ii",
      "choices": ["I", "ii", "IV", "V"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Top-level fields

| Field              | Type   | Default    | Description                                                  |
|--------------------|--------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `type`             | string | —          | Must be `"identification"`.                                  |
| `identMode`        | string | `"submit"` | Feedback mode — see below.                                   |
| `key`              | string | `"jC_"`    | Key signature code (same format as other exercise types).    |
| `staffDistribution`| string | `"keyboard"` | Staff layout (same choices as chord exercises).            |

### Per-chord fields (`chord` array)

Each entry in `chord` represents one problem (one notated chord with a question mark below it).

| Field     | Type     | Required | Description                                              |
|-----------|----------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `notes`   | int[]    | yes      | MIDI pitches to display. All notes are shown (no hidden).|
| `answer`  | string   | yes      | The single correct label.                                |
| `choices` | string[] | yes      | All options shown in the popup (should include the answer). |

---

## Feedback Modes (`identMode`)

| Value      | Behaviour                                                                                     |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `"submit"` | Student picks all answers, then clicks **Submit**. Correct (green ✓) / wrong (red ✗) revealed only after Submit. |
| `"practice"` | Correct/incorrect shown immediately after each selection (green or red). Exercise auto-completes if all correct. |
| `"test"`   | Answers are locked after selecting — no colour feedback shown at all. Exercise auto-submits silently once every slot is answered. |

---

## UX Behaviour

- A grey **?** label is drawn below the bass staff for each chord, at the same x/y position as Roman numeral annotations (`bass.getStartX() + 8`, `bass.getBottomY() + 18`).
- The cursor changes to a pointer only when hovering over a label zone (the 60 px strip below the bottom of each bass staff column).
- Clicking inside that zone opens a small popup listing the available choices.
- After selection the label turns dark; after grading it turns green (correct) or red (incorrect) with a ✓ or ✗ below it.
- In **test** mode, once a slot is answered subsequent clicks on it are ignored.
- Analysis overlays (Roman numerals, figured bass, chord symbols) are always hidden for identification exercises — the overlay would give away the answers.

---

## Admin

In the Django admin, open an exercise whose `data.type` is `"identification"`. The form:

- Hides the "Assessment method" radio group (type is fixed).
- Hides fields that don't apply: rhythm, visibility pattern, time signature, semibreves per line, staff distribution.
- Shows an **Identification settings** fieldset with:
  - **Feedback mode** (`identMode`) — RadioSelect with submit / practice / test options.

To create a new identification exercise, edit the JSON `data` field directly (the raw editor at the bottom of the change form), set `type` to `"identification"`, and save. The form will then detect the type and show the Identification settings fieldset on subsequent edits.

---

## Key Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [lab/static/js/src/models/identification_grader.js](../lab/static/js/src/models/identification_grader.js) | Stores answers, grades against `problem.answer` per slot |
| [lab/static/js/src/components/music/exercise_sheet.js](../lab/static/js/src/components/music/exercise_sheet.js) | `initIdentificationMode`, `_showIdentPopup`, `drawIdentificationLabels`, `onSubmitIdentification` |
| [lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_definition.js](../lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_definition.js) | `isIdentification()`, `getIdentMode()`, chord normalisation for identification type |
| [lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_context.js](../lab/static/js/src/models/exercise_context.js) | Bypasses chord-bank advancement; treats result from grader as flawless pass |
| [apps/exercises/forms.py](../apps/exercises/forms.py) | `_detect_identification`, `_configure_identification_fields`, `_store_identification_settings` |
| [apps/exercises/admin.py](../apps/exercises/admin.py) | Injects "Identification settings" fieldset when `data.type == "identification"` |

---

## Data Flow

```
Exercise.data (Django DB)
    ↓  served as JSON to the browser
ExerciseDefinition.parse()
    → normalises each chord entry: all notes go to visible[], hidden=[]
    → copies answer and choices onto the problem object
    → reads identMode
    ↓
ExerciseSheet.initIdentificationMode()
    → attaches click + mousemove handlers to canvas
    → shows/hides #identification-actions Submit button based on mode
    ↓
Student clicks label zone → _showIdentPopup()
    → IdentificationGrader.setAnswer(index, choice)
    → mode branch: practice (grade + render), test (render + auto-submit), submit (render)
    ↓
onSubmitIdentification() / auto-submit
    → IdentificationGrader.grade(definition) → {result, score, problems[]}
    → exerciseContext.graded = graded
    → render() → drawIdentificationLabels() colours labels + draws ✓/✗
    → if result === "correct": setTimeout → exerciseContext.grade() → advance/complete
```

---

## Grading Logic (`IdentificationGrader.grade`)

- Iterates over `definition.getProblems()`.
- For each problem, compares `answers[i]` (student choice) against `problem.answer`.
- `correct: true` → green ✓; `correct: false` → red ✗; `correct: null` → not yet answered.
- `result`:
  - `"correct"` — all slots answered and all correct
  - `"incorrect"` — all slots answered but at least one wrong
  - `"partial"` — some slots still unanswered
- `score`: `0` correct, `1` partial, `2` incorrect.

In **test** mode, `exerciseContext.graded` is never set before submission, so `drawIdentificationLabels` never renders colour feedback regardless of the grader's output.

- [ ] Add `/dashboard/exercises/audit/` — paginated table of all exercises by current user
- [ ] Columns: ID, description, key, type, tags, playlist count, locked, created date
- [ ] Filter by type, tag, key; full-text search on description
- [ ] Inline quick-edit for description and tags (no page reload)
- [ ] Bulk-tag action
- [ ] Links to exercise editor and preview from each row
- [ ] find a way to allow a teacher to work on a single course or single playlist not seeing all the exercises but only the ones that already belong to those courses or playlists. 

### 2.20 Streamlined exercise creation flow

Currently 3 pages: (1) MIDI input, (2) save/type form, (3) preview. Friction kills content velocity.

- [ ] After saving from play/MIDI page, land on exercise editor with notes pre-populated — skip the middle confirm page
- [ ] Type, analysis settings, description all editable on the same page as the staff preview
- [ ] "Save and create another" action that resets input without navigating away
- [ ] Side-by-side layout: staff preview left, settings panel right

### 2.21 Smart playlist transposition ✅ DONE

Transposition always goes up — C→Bb shifts up a major 7th instead of down a major 2nd. Exercises end up in wrong registers.

- [x] Find where transposition interval is computed (`apps/exercises/utils/transpose.py`)
- [x] For each target key, pick the direction that results in the smaller interval (≤ 6 semitones)
- [x] Tritone (exactly 6 semitones): prefer down
- [x] Tests: C→F = +5 (up P4), C→Bb = −2 (down M2), C→F# = −6 (down tritone), C→G = −5 (down P4)
- [x] All 12×12 key pairs verified: no vector exceeds 6 semitones

### 2.22 Curriculum assembly tool

_Needs spec session before implementation._

No bird's-eye view of a course under construction. Everything is separate edit pages.

- [ ] Spec the UI
- [ ] Course outline page: available playlists/exercises left, course structure right
- [ ] Drag-and-drop reordering of playlists in course and exercises in playlist
- [ ] Inline new-playlist creation
- [ ] Transposition settings visible + editable per playlist inline
- [ ] Publish/unpublish from this view

---

## Phase 3 — Monetization

_Start after pilot validates the product._

### 3.1 Role field + teacher verification
- [ ] Add `role` field (`student` / `teacher`), role selector on registration, `.edu` gate + manual approval path

### 3.2 Email verification
- [ ] New accounts `is_active=False`; send signed verification link on registration; link sets `is_active=True`

### 3.3 Stripe integration
- [ ] `stripe_subscription_id` + `subscription_status` on User; Checkout in group join flow; payment success webhook → enroll; subscription management page

### 3.4 Access control
- [ ] Subscription check decorator; gate: group join, performance submission in course context, gradebook; free: library, solo practice, own content

---

## Phase 4 — Growth

_Prioritise based on pilot feedback._

- [ ] Species counterpoint exercise type
- [ ] Harmonic dictation exercise type
- [ ] Melodic dictation exercise type
- [ ] Frontend: replace RequireJS with Vite
- [ ] Frontend: Bootstrap 4 → 5 (or Tailwind)
- [ ] Frontend: add htmx for partial-page updates
