from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import SimpleTestCase, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from apps.exercises.models import (
    Course,
    Exercise,
    PerformanceData,
    Playlist,
    PlaylistCourseOrdered,
    RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress,
)
from apps.exercises.utils.recurrence import (
    count_playlist_cycles,
    get_assignment_period_bounds,
    rebuild_period_progress,
)

User = get_user_model()


class RecurringAssignmentPeriodBoundsTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def test_daily_period_returns_calendar_day_boundaries(self):
        """Daily recurrence always returns midnight-to-midnight for the calendar day of
        occurred_at in the project timezone, regardless of the anchor time.
        """
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            recurrence_starts_on=datetime(2026, 4, 1, 15, 30),
        )
        occurred_at = timezone.make_aware(
            datetime(2026, 4, 3, 2, 45),
            timezone.get_current_timezone(),
        )

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        self.assertEqual(period_start.tzinfo, timezone.get_current_timezone())
        self.assertEqual(period_end.tzinfo, timezone.get_current_timezone())
        self.assertEqual(
            period_start,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 3, 0, 0), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            period_end,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 4, 0, 0), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )

    def test_weekly_period_uses_recurrence_starts_on_as_anchor(self):
        """When recurrence_starts_on is set it takes precedence over publish_date."""
        anchor = datetime(2026, 4, 1, 8, 0)  # Wednesday; local wall-clock
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            recurrence_starts_on=anchor,
            publish_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0),  # earlier date — must be ignored
        )
        occurred_at = timezone.make_aware(
            datetime(2026, 4, 12, 10, 0),  # 11 days after anchor → 2nd week
            timezone.get_current_timezone(),
        )

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        self.assertEqual(
            period_start,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 8, 8, 0), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            period_end,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 8, 0), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )

    def test_weekly_period_is_seven_days_from_anchor(self):
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            publish_date=datetime(2026, 4, 2, 10, 15),
            recurrence_starts_on=None,
        )
        occurred_at = timezone.make_aware(
            datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0),
            timezone.get_current_timezone(),
        )

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        self.assertEqual(
            period_start,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 15), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            period_end,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 16, 10, 15), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )

    def test_weekly_no_anchor_falls_back_to_occurred_at(self):
        """When both recurrence_starts_on and publish_date are absent, occurred_at
        becomes the anchor, so the period runs from occurred_at to +7 days.
        """
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            recurrence_starts_on=None,
            publish_date=None,
        )
        occurred_at = timezone.make_aware(
            datetime(2026, 4, 9, 14, 0),
            timezone.get_current_timezone(),
        )

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        self.assertEqual(period_start, occurred_at)
        self.assertEqual(
            period_end,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 16, 14, 0), timezone.get_current_timezone()),
        )

    def test_publish_date_fallback_uses_local_wallclock(self):
        """publish_date used as anchor must be treated as local wall-clock, not UTC.

        The codebase convention (publish_dates_dict, due_dates_dict) is to call
        .replace(tzinfo=settings.TIME_ZONE) on stored publish_date values because
        they are authored as local times, not stored as UTC offsets.  Verify that
        an aware UTC-stamped publish_date produces a period whose anchor hour is
        the original stored hour in local time (10:15), NOT the UTC→local conversion
        result (06:15 in America/New_York which is UTC-4 in April).
        """
        ny_tz = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
        # Simulate what Django returns from the DB with USE_TZ=True: a UTC-aware value
        # whose numeric hour matches what the author typed (local wall-clock).
        utc_aware_publish_date = datetime(2026, 4, 2, 10, 15, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            publish_date=utc_aware_publish_date,
            recurrence_starts_on=None,
        )
        occurred_at = datetime(2026, 4, 3, 12, 0, tzinfo=ny_tz)

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        # Wall-clock convention: anchor = 2026-04-02 10:15 NY (not 06:15 NY)
        # A UTC→local conversion would yield 06:15; .replace() gives 10:15.
        expected_start = datetime(2026, 4, 2, 10, 15, tzinfo=ny_tz)
        expected_end = datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 15, tzinfo=ny_tz)
        self.assertEqual(
            period_start.astimezone(ny_tz).replace(tzinfo=None),
            expected_start.replace(tzinfo=None),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            period_end.astimezone(ny_tz).replace(tzinfo=None),
            expected_end.replace(tzinfo=None),
        )

    def test_daily_dst_spring_forward(self):
        """Daily period boundaries must land on calendar midnight across DST spring-forward.

        America/New_York springs forward on 2026-03-08 (02:00 → 03:00).  An event on
        2026-03-09 (the day after) anchored to a pre-DST date must still begin at
        00:00 local time, not at 01:00 which fixed-timedelta stepping would produce.
        """
        ny_tz = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered(
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            # Anchor is in EST (UTC-5); Mar 9 is now in EDT (UTC-4)
            recurrence_starts_on=datetime(2026, 3, 7, 0, 0, tzinfo=ny_tz),
        )
        occurred_at = datetime(2026, 3, 9, 10, 0, tzinfo=ny_tz)

        period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

        local_start = period_start.astimezone(ny_tz).replace(tzinfo=None)
        local_end = period_end.astimezone(ny_tz).replace(tzinfo=None)
        # Both boundaries must be at 00:00 (not 01:00) on the expected dates
        self.assertEqual(local_start, datetime(2026, 3, 9, 0, 0))
        self.assertEqual(local_end, datetime(2026, 3, 10, 0, 0))


class RecurringCycleCountingTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def test_count_playlist_cycles_uses_set_semantics_for_cycle_requirements(self):
        exercise_ids = ["EA0001", "EA0001", "EA0002"]
        attempts = [
            {
                "id": "EA0001-A",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 9, 0)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0002-A",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 9, 1)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
        ]

        counted_passes, first_pass_at, last_counted_pass_at = count_playlist_cycles(
            exercise_ids,
            attempts,
            cap=99,
        )

        self.assertEqual(counted_passes, 1)
        self.assertEqual(first_pass_at, attempts[1]["performed_at"])
        self.assertEqual(last_counted_pass_at, attempts[1]["performed_at"])

    def test_count_playlist_cycles_consumes_error_free_attempts_greedily(self):
        exercise_ids = ["EA0001", "EA0002", "EA0003"]
        attempts = [
            {
                "id": "EA0001-T1",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 0)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },

                "id": "EA0002-X",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 1)),
                "error_tally": None,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0001-Y",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 2)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0003-Z",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 3)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0002-A",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 4)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0001-B",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 5)),
                "error_tally": 2,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0003-C",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 6)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0001-D",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 10, 7)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
        ]

        counted_passes, first_pass_at, last_counted_pass_at = count_playlist_cycles(
            exercise_ids,
            attempts,
            cap=99,
        )

        self.assertEqual(counted_passes, 2)
        self.assertEqual(first_pass_at, attempts[3]["performed_at"])
        self.assertEqual(last_counted_pass_at, attempts[7]["performed_at"])

    def test_count_playlist_cycles_caps_the_result(self):
        exercise_ids = ["EA0001", "EA0002"]
        attempts = [
            {
                "id": "EA0001-1",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 0)),
                "error_tally": 0,

                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 1)),
                "error_tally": 0,

            {
                "id": "EA0001-2",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 2)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0002-2",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 3)),
                "error_tally": 0,
            },
            {
                "id": "EA0001-3",
                "performed_at": timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 4)),
                "error_tally": 0,

                "id": "EA0002-3",

    def test_count_playlist_cycles_skips_malformed_attempt_entries(self):

        attempts = [

class RecurringProgressRebuildTests(SimpleTestCase):
    @patch("apps.exercises.models.RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.update_or_create")
    def test_rebuild_period_progress_treats_naive_performed_at_as_utc(self, update_or_create_mock):
        ny_tz = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
        update_or_create_mock.return_value = (SimpleNamespace(), True)

        assignment = SimpleNamespace(
            RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            recurrence_starts_on=None,
            publish_date=None,
            required_passes_per_period=1,
            course=SimpleNamespace(id=123),
            playlist=SimpleNamespace(exercise_list=["EA0001"]),
        )

        performance_data = SimpleNamespace(
            user=SimpleNamespace(id=456),
            playlist=assignment.playlist,
            data=[
                # Naive string interpreted as UTC => 2026-04-08 23:59:59 NY (outside period)
                {"id": "EA0001-OLD", "performed_at": "2026-04-09T03:59:59", "error_tally": 0},
                # Naive string interpreted as UTC => 2026-04-09 00:00:00 NY (period start)
                {"id": "EA0001-NEW", "performed_at": "2026-04-09T04:00:00", "error_tally": 0},
            ],
        )

        with timezone.override("America/New_York"):
            occurred_at = datetime(2026, 4, 9, 12, 0, tzinfo=ny_tz)
            rebuild_period_progress(assignment, performance_data, occurred_at)

        defaults = update_or_create_mock.call_args.kwargs["defaults"]
        expected_first_pass = datetime(2026, 4, 9, 0, 0, tzinfo=ny_tz)
        self.assertEqual(defaults["counted_passes"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(defaults["first_pass_at"], expected_first_pass)

    @patch("apps.exercises.models.RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.update_or_create")
    def test_rebuild_period_progress_skips_malformed_attempt_entries(self, update_or_create_mock):
        update_or_create_mock.return_value = (SimpleNamespace(), True)

        assignment = SimpleNamespace(
            RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            recurrence_starts_on=None,
            publish_date=None,
            required_passes_per_period=1,
            course=SimpleNamespace(id=321),
            playlist=SimpleNamespace(exercise_list=["EA0001"]),
        )

        valid_performed_at = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 13, 0))
        performance_data = SimpleNamespace(
            user=SimpleNamespace(id=654),
            playlist=assignment.playlist,
            data=[
                None,
                "not-a-dict",
                42,
                {"id": "EA0001-A", "performed_at": "not-a-datetime", "error_tally": 0},
                {"id": "EA0001-B", "error_tally": 0},
                {"id": "EA0001-C", "performed_at": valid_performed_at, "error_tally": 0},
            ],
        )

        occurred_at = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 14, 0))
        rebuild_period_progress(assignment, performance_data, occurred_at)

        defaults = update_or_create_mock.call_args.kwargs["defaults"]
        self.assertEqual(defaults["counted_passes"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(defaults["first_pass_at"], valid_performed_at)


class RecurringSubmitFlowTests(TestCase):
    def _build_assignment(self, is_recurring, required_passes_per_period=1):
        author = User.objects.create_user(
            email="author@example.com",
            password="test-pass-123",
        )
        performer = User.objects.create_user(
            email="performer@example.com",
            password="test-pass-123",
        )
        exercise = Exercise(
            authored_by=author,
            data={},
        )
        exercise.save()
        playlist = Playlist(
            authored_by=author,
            name="Recurring Playlist",
        )
        playlist.save()
        playlist.exercises.add(exercise, through_defaults={"order": 1})
        course = Course(
            authored_by=author,
            title="Recurring Course",
        )
        course.save()
        assignment = PlaylistCourseOrdered.objects.create(
            playlist=playlist,
            course=course,
            order=1,
            is_recurring=is_recurring,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY if is_recurring else "",
            required_passes_per_period=required_passes_per_period,
            recurrence_starts_on=timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 0, 0)) if is_recurring else None,
        )
        return performer, exercise, playlist, course, assignment

    @patch("apps.exercises.models.Course.add_performance_to_dict")
    def test_submit_uses_single_timestamp_for_payload_and_rebuild_boundary(
        self,
        _add_performance_to_dict_mock,
    ):
        before_boundary = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 23, 59, 59))
        after_boundary = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 10, 0, 0, 0))

        performer, exercise, playlist, course, _assignment = self._build_assignment(
            is_recurring=True,
            required_passes_per_period=1,
        )

        with patch("apps.exercises.models.now") as now_mock:
            now_mock.side_effect = [before_boundary, after_boundary]
            PerformanceData.submit(
                user_id=performer.id,
                course_id=course._id,
                playlist_id=playlist._id,
                exercise_id=exercise.id,
                data={"error_tally": 0},
            )

        progress = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.get(
            user=performer,
            course=course,
            playlist=playlist,
        )
        progress_period_start_local = timezone.localtime(progress.period_start)
        progress_period_end_local = timezone.localtime(progress.period_end)
        self.assertEqual(
            progress_period_start_local,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 0, 0, 0)),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            progress_period_end_local,
            timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 10, 0, 0, 0)),
        )
        self.assertEqual(progress.counted_passes, 1)

        pd = PerformanceData.objects.get(
            user=performer,
            playlist=playlist,
            course=course,
        )
        self.assertEqual(pd.data[-1]["performed_at"], "2026-04-09 23:59:59")

    @patch("apps.exercises.models.Course.add_performance_to_dict")
    @patch("apps.exercises.models.now")
    def test_submit_refreshes_recurring_progress_for_recurring_assignments(
        self,
        now_mock,
        _add_performance_to_dict_mock,
    ):
        now_mock.return_value = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 9, 0))
        performer, exercise, playlist, course, _assignment = self._build_assignment(
            is_recurring=True,
            required_passes_per_period=2,
        )

        PerformanceData.submit(
            user_id=performer.id,
            course_id=course._id,
            playlist_id=playlist._id,
            exercise_id=exercise.id,
            data={"error_tally": 0},
        )

        self.assertEqual(RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.count(), 1)
        progress = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.get(
            user=performer,
            course=course,
            playlist=playlist,
        )
        self.assertEqual(progress.counted_passes, 1)
        self.assertFalse(progress.target_met)

        now_mock.return_value = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 9, 5))
        PerformanceData.submit(
            user_id=performer.id,
            course_id=course._id,
            playlist_id=playlist._id,
            exercise_id=exercise.id,
            data={"error_tally": 0},
        )

        self.assertEqual(RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.count(), 1)
        progress.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(progress.counted_passes, 2)
        self.assertTrue(progress.target_met)

    @patch("apps.exercises.models.Course.add_performance_to_dict")
    @patch("apps.exercises.models.now")
    def test_submit_leaves_non_recurring_assignments_without_progress_rows(

    @patch("apps.exercises.models.Course.add_performance_to_dict")
    @patch("apps.exercises.models.now")
    def test_submit_uses_deterministic_assignment_order_when_duplicates_exist(
        self,
        now_mock,
        _add_performance_to_dict_mock,
    ):
        now_mock.return_value = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 11, 0))
        performer, exercise, playlist, course, assignment = self._build_assignment(
            is_recurring=True,
            required_passes_per_period=1,
        )
        assignment.order = 2
        assignment.required_passes_per_period = 1
        assignment.save()

        # Duplicate assignment rows can exist historically; submit() should pick the
        # deterministic first row by (order, pk), i.e. this one with order=1.
        PlaylistCourseOrdered.objects.create(
            playlist=playlist,
            course=course,
            order=1,
            is_recurring=True,
            recurrence_unit=PlaylistCourseOrdered.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY,
            required_passes_per_period=2,
            recurrence_starts_on=timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 9, 0, 0)),
        )

        PerformanceData.submit(
            user_id=performer.id,
            course_id=course._id,
            playlist_id=playlist._id,
            exercise_id=exercise.id,
            data={"error_tally": 0},
        )

        progress = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.get(
            user=performer,
            course=course,
            playlist=playlist,
        )
        self.assertEqual(progress.required_passes, 2)
        self.assertEqual(progress.counted_passes, 1)
        self.assertFalse(progress.target_met)

apps/exercises/management/commands/truncate_timestamps.py
File type: .py
from django.core.management import BaseCommand
from django.db import connections

from apps.exercises.models import PerformanceData, Exercise, Playlist, Course


class Command(BaseCommand):
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        models = [Exercise, Playlist, Course, PerformanceData]
        with connections["default"].cursor() as cursor:
            for model in models:
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE {} "
                    "SET created = DATE_TRUNC('second', created), updated = DATE_TRUNC('second', updated) ".format(
                        model._meta.db_table
                    )
                )
        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS("Successfully removed microseconds from timestamps.")
        )

apps/exercises/management/commands/duplicate_chorale_as_identification.py
File type: .py
import copy

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError

from apps.exercises.models import Exercise

User = get_user_model()


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Duplicate an existing chorale exercise as a chorale_identification exercise"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument("exercise_id", type=str, help="ID of the source chorale exercise")
        parser.add_argument("--author", type=str, required=True, help="Email of the exercise author")
        parser.add_argument(
            "--analysis",
            choices=["roman", "figured_bass"],
            default="roman",
            help="Analysis label type for the new identification exercise",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--public",
            action="store_true",
            help="Set new exercise as public (defaults to source visibility)",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        exercise_id = options["exercise_id"]
        author_email = options["author"]
        analysis = options["analysis"]
        force_public = options["public"]

        try:
            author = User.objects.get(email=author_email)
        except User.DoesNotExist:
            raise CommandError(f'User with email "{author_email}" not found')

        try:
            source = Exercise.objects.get(id=exercise_id)
        except Exercise.DoesNotExist:
            raise CommandError(f'Exercise with id "{exercise_id}" not found')

        source_data = source.data or {}
        if source_data.get("type") != "chorale":
            raise CommandError("Source exercise must have data.type='chorale'")

        score = copy.deepcopy(source_data.get("score", {}))
        if not score:
            raise CommandError("Source exercise is missing score data")

        new_data = {
            "type": "chorale_identification",
            "identMode": "submit",
            "analysisType": analysis,
            "score": score,
            "key": source_data.get("key") or score.get("meta", {}).get("key", "C"),
            "staffDistribution": "chorale",
            "introText": source_data.get("introText") or "Label the harmony for each onset.",
            "reviewText": source_data.get("reviewText") or "Well done!",
        }

        # Exercise.save() performs a custom two-step save; avoid objects.create(force_insert=True).
        new_exercise = Exercise(
            description=f"{source.description or source.id} (identification)",
            data=new_data,
            authored_by=author,
            is_public=True if force_public else source.is_public,
        )
        new_exercise.save()

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(
                f"Created chorale_identification exercise {new_exercise.id} from source {source.id}"
            )
        )

apps/exercises/management/commands/import_chorale.py
File type: .py
"""
Management command to import a single chorale as an exercise.

Usage:
  python manage.py import_chorale <corpus_file> --author=<email>

Example:
  python manage.py import_chorale bwv1.6.json --author=admin@example.com
"""
import json
import os
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from apps.exercises.models import Exercise

User = get_user_model()


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = 'Import a chorale from data/corpus/bach as an Exercise'

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument('corpus_file', type=str, help='Filename in data/corpus/bach/')
        parser.add_argument('--author', type=str, required=True, help='Email of the exercise author')
        parser.add_argument('--start', type=int, default=0, help='Start measure (0-indexed)')
        parser.add_argument('--end', type=int, default=4, help='End measure (exclusive)')
        parser.add_argument('--mode', choices=['play', 'identify'], default='play', help='Exercise creation mode')
        parser.add_argument('--analysis', choices=['roman', 'figured_bass', 'interval_generic', 'interval_specific'], default='roman', help='Analysis label type for identify mode')
        parser.add_argument('--compound', action='store_true', default=False, help='Allow compound intervals (default: reduce to within octave). Only applies to interval analysis types.')
        parser.add_argument('--public', action='store_true', help='Make the exercise public')

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        corpus_file = options['corpus_file']
        author_email = options['author']
        start_measure = options['start']
        end_measure = options['end']
        mode = options['mode']
        analysis_type = options['analysis']
        compound = options['compound']
        is_public = options['public']

        # Find the author
        try:
            author = User.objects.get(email=author_email)
        except User.DoesNotExist:
            raise CommandError(f'User with email "{author_email}" not found')

        # Load the corpus JSON
        corpus_path = os.path.join('data', 'corpus', 'bach', corpus_file)
        if not os.path.exists(corpus_path):
            raise CommandError(f'Corpus file not found: {corpus_path}')

        with open(corpus_path, 'r') as f:
            corpus_data = json.load(f)

        score = corpus_data.get('score', {})
        meta = score.get('meta', {})
        measures = score.get('measures', [])

        if not measures:
            raise CommandError('No measures found in corpus file')

        # Extract excerpt
        excerpt_measures = measures[start_measure:end_measure]
        if not excerpt_measures:
            raise CommandError(f'No measures in range [{start_measure}:{end_measure}]')

        def count_voices(selected_measures):
            if not selected_measures:
                return 0
            first = selected_measures[0].get('staves', {})
            return sum(len(stave.get('voices', [])) for stave in first.values())

        if analysis_type in ('interval_generic', 'interval_specific'):
            voice_count = count_voices(excerpt_measures)
            if voice_count != 2:
                raise CommandError(
                    f'Interval identification requires exactly 2 voices; '
                    f'found {voice_count} in {corpus_file}.'
                )

        # Build exercise data
        bwv = corpus_file.replace('.json', '').upper()
        title = f"{bwv} (mm. {start_measure+1}–{end_measure})"

        if mode == 'identify':
            if analysis_type == 'roman':
                analysis_label = 'Roman numerals'
            elif analysis_type == 'figured_bass':
                analysis_label = 'figured bass'
            elif analysis_type == 'interval_generic':
                analysis_label = 'generic intervals'
            else:
                analysis_label = 'specific intervals'

            if analysis_type in ('interval_generic', 'interval_specific'):
                intro = f"Identify the {analysis_label} in this two-voice excerpt of {bwv}, measures {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}."
            else:
                intro = f"Label the {analysis_label} for {bwv}, measures {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}."

            exercise_data = {
                "type": "chorale_identification",
                "identMode": "submit",
                "analysisType": analysis_type,
                "compoundIntervals": compound,
                "score": {
                    "meta": meta,
                    "measures": excerpt_measures
                },
                "introText": intro,
                "reviewText": f"Well done! You completed {bwv}, measures {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}.",
                "key": meta.get("key", "C"),
                "staffDistribution": "chorale"
            }
            title = f"{bwv} identification ({analysis_type}, mm. {start_measure+1}–{end_measure})"
        else:
            exercise_data = {
                "type": "chorale",
                "mode": "play-all-voices",
                "score": {
                    "meta": meta,
                    "measures": excerpt_measures
                },
                "targetVoices": "all",
                "display": {
                    "showFigures": False,
                    "showRomans": False,
                    "transpose": 0,
                    "tempo": 60
                },
                "grading": {
                    "onsetWindowMs": 150,
                    "releaseTolerancePct": 40,
                    "octaveFlexible": False
                },
                "excerpt": {
                    "startMeasure": start_measure,
                    "endMeasure": end_measure
                },
                "introText": f"Play all four voices of {bwv}, measures {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}. Use the keyboard or MIDI controller to play each note as it appears. Notes turn black when played correctly.",
                "reviewText": f"Well done! You completed {bwv}, measures {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}.",
                # Legacy fields for compatibility
                "key": meta.get("key", "C"),
                "keySignature": meta.get("key", "C"),
                "staffDistribution": "chorale"
            }

        # Create the Exercise
        exercise = Exercise(
            description=title,
            data=exercise_data,
            authored_by=author,
            is_public=is_public
        )
        exercise.save()

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f'Successfully created exercise {exercise.id}: {title}'
        ))
        self.stdout.write(f'  Measures: {len(excerpt_measures)}')
        self.stdout.write(f'  Key: {meta.get("key", "?")}')
        self.stdout.write(f'  Time: {meta.get("time", "?")}')

apps/exercises/management/commands/migrate_exercises.py
File type: .py
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.management import BaseCommand

from apps.exercises.models import Playlist, Exercise

User = get_user_model()


class CustomExerciseRepo(ExerciseRepository):
    def getGroupList(self):
        return sorted(
            [
                {
                    "name": g.name,
                    "size": g.size(),
                }
                for g in self.groups
                if len(g.name) > 0
            ],
            key=lambda g: g["name"].lower(),
        )


class Command(BaseCommand):
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        repository = CustomExerciseRepo.create()
        for group in repository.getGroupList():
            if Playlist.objects.filter(name=group["name"]).exists():
                continue
            playlist = Playlist()
            playlist.name = group["name"]
            playlist.authored_by = User.objects.filter(is_superuser=True).first()
            playlist.exercises = ""
            playlist.save()

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(
                "%s playlists are successfully created." % Playlist.objects.count()
            )
        )

        for repo_exercise in repository.exercises:
            repo_exercise.load()
            exercise = Exercise()
            exercise.data = repo_exercise.exerciseDefinition.data
            exercise.is_public = True
            exercise.authored_by = User.objects.filter(is_superuser=True).first()
            exercise.save()

            playlist = Playlist.objects.filter(
                name=repo_exercise.getGroupName()
            ).first()
            if playlist.exercises == "":
                playlist.exercises = exercise.id
            else:
                playlist.exercises = playlist.exercises + "," + exercise.id
            playlist.save()

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(
                "%s exercises are successfully created and assigned to proper playlists."
                % Exercise.objects.count()
            )
        )

File End

apps/exercises/management/commands/import_musicxml.py
File type: .py
"""
Management command to import a MusicXML file as an exercise.

Usage:
  python manage.py import_musicxml <path_to_file.xml> --author=<email>

Example:
  python manage.py import_musicxml ~/Desktop/mypiece.musicxml --author=admin@example.com
"""
import json
import os
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model

# Import the converter from the fetch_bach_chorales script
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '../../../../scripts'))
try:
    from fetch_bach_chorales import m21_to_cir, build_events
except ImportError:
    m21_to_cir = None
    build_events = None

from apps.exercises.models import Exercise

User = get_user_model()


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = 'Import a MusicXML file as an Exercise using music21 → CIR pipeline'

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument('file_path', type=str, help='Path to MusicXML file (.xml or .musicxml)')
        parser.add_argument('--author', type=str, required=True, help='Email of the exercise author')
        parser.add_argument('--title', type=str, help='Exercise title (defaults to filename)')
        parser.add_argument('--public', action='store_true', help='Make the exercise public')
        parser.add_argument('--start', type=int, default=0, help='Start measure (0-indexed, default: 0)')
        parser.add_argument('--end', type=int, default=None, help='End measure (exclusive, default: all)')

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        file_path = options['file_path']
        author_email = options['author']
        title = options.get('title')
        is_public = options['public']
        start_measure = options['start']
        end_measure = options['end']

        # Check dependencies
        if m21_to_cir is None or build_events is None:
            raise CommandError(
                'Could not import converter functions. Make sure music21 is installed: '
                'pip install music21'
            )

        try:
            from music21 import converter
        except ImportError:
            raise CommandError(
                'music21 is not installed. Install it with: pip install music21'
            )

        # Find the author
        try:
            author = User.objects.get(email=author_email)
        except User.DoesNotExist:
            raise CommandError(f'User with email "{author_email}" not found')

        # Check file exists
        if not os.path.exists(file_path):
            raise CommandError(f'File not found: {file_path}')

        # Check file extension
        ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1].lower()
        if ext not in ['.xml', '.musicxml', '.mxl']:
            raise CommandError(f'File must be a MusicXML file (.xml, .musicxml, or .mxl)')

        # Load MusicXML with music21
        self.stdout.write(f'Loading MusicXML file: {file_path}')
        try:
            score = converter.parse(file_path)
        except Exception as e:
            raise CommandError(f'Failed to parse MusicXML: {str(e)}')

        # Convert to CIR (Canonical Internal Representation)
        self.stdout.write('Converting to internal format...')
        try:
            cir = m21_to_cir(score)
        except Exception as e:
            raise CommandError(f'Failed to convert to CIR: {str(e)}')

        # Get metadata
        meta = cir.get('meta', {})
        measures = cir.get('measures', [])

        if not measures:
            raise CommandError('No measures found in MusicXML file')

        # Extract excerpt if specified
        if end_measure is not None:
            excerpt_measures = measures[start_measure:end_measure]
            measure_range = f"mm. {start_measure+1}–{end_measure}"
        else:
            excerpt_measures = measures[start_measure:]
            measure_range = f"mm. {start_measure+1}–{len(measures)}" if start_measure > 0 else f"complete ({len(measures)} measures)"

        if not excerpt_measures:
            raise CommandError(f'No measures in range [{start_measure}:{end_measure}]')

        # Generate title from filename if not provided
        if not title:
            basename = os.path.basename(file_path)
            name_without_ext = os.path.splitext(basename)[0]
            title = f"{name_without_ext} ({measure_range})" if start_measure > 0 or end_measure else name_without_ext

        # Build exercise data structure
        exercise_data = {
            "type": "musicxml",
            "mode": "play-all-voices",
            "score": {
                "meta": meta,
                "measures": excerpt_measures
            },
            "source": {
                "type": "musicxml",
                "filename": os.path.basename(file_path),
                "originalPath": file_path,
                "imported": True
            },
            "targetVoices": "all",
            "display": {
                "showFigures": False,
                "showRomans": False,
                "transpose": 0,
                "tempo": 60
            },
            "grading": {
                "onsetWindowMs": 150,
                "releaseTolerancePct": 40,
                "octaveFlexible": False
            },
            "excerpt": {
                "startMeasure": start_measure,
                "endMeasure": end_measure if end_measure else len(measures)
            },
            "introText": f"Play {title}.",
            "reviewText": "Good work!",
            # Legacy fields for compatibility
            "key": meta.get("key", "C"),
            "keySignature": meta.get("key", "C"),
            "staffDistribution": "chorale"
        }

        # Optionally build events timeline for grading
        try:
            events = build_events(cir)
            if events:
                exercise_data["events"] = [
                    {
                        "start": e.start,
                        "perStaff": e.perStaff
                    }
                    for e in events
                ]
                self.stdout.write(f'  Generated {len(events)} grading events')
        except Exception as e:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(f'  Could not generate events: {str(e)}'))

        # Create the Exercise
        exercise = Exercise(
            description=title,
            data=exercise_data,
            authored_by=author,
            is_public=is_public
        )
        exercise.save()

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f'\nSuccessfully created exercise {exercise.id}: {title}'
        ))
        self.stdout.write(f'  Measures: {len(excerpt_measures)}')
        self.stdout.write(f'  Key: {meta.get("key", "?")}')
        self.stdout.write(f'  Time: {meta.get("time", "?")}')
        self.stdout.write(f'  Public: {is_public}')
        self.stdout.write(f'\n  View at: /lab/exercise/{exercise.id}')


--------------------------------------------------
File End

apps/exercises/management/commands/set_exercise_locks.py
File type: .py
from django.core.management import BaseCommand

from apps.exercises.models import PerformanceData, Exercise


class Command(BaseCommand):
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        performed_exercises = {}
        performances = PerformanceData.objects.all()

        for performance in performances:
            for exercise in performance.data:
                performed_exercises.setdefault(exercise["id"], [])
                performed_exercises[exercise["id"]].append(performance.user_id)
        performed_exercises = {k: list(set(v)) for k, v in performed_exercises.items()}

        """
        Sample output structure for performed_exercises:
        {
            'EA00CI': [2, 3], 
            'EA00CJ': [2, 3], 
            'EA00CK': [2, 3], 
            'EA00CL': [2, 3], 
            'EA00CI1': [2]       # transposed
        }
        values are the user ids that have performed the exercise
        """

        locked_exercises = 0
        for exercise in Exercise.objects.all():
            if exercise.locked:
                continue

            for key, value in performed_exercises.items():
                if (
                    exercise.id not in key
                ):  # filtering for regular and transposed exercises
                    continue

                # if more than one users have performed exercise, or if only one user did and it is not the author of exercise
                if len(value) > 1 or (
                    len(value) == 1 and value != exercise.authored_by_id
                ):
                    exercise.locked = True
                    exercise.save()
                    locked_exercises += 1

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(
                f"{locked_exercises} exercises has been successfully locked."
            )
        )

apps/exercises/utils/recurrence.py
File type: .py
import math
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from django.conf import settings
from django.utils import timezone
from django.utils.dateparse import parse_datetime


def _to_project_timezone(value):
    """Convert an aware or naive datetime to the project timezone via proper UTC conversion."""
    project_tz = ZoneInfo(settings.TIME_ZONE)
    if timezone.is_naive(value):
        return timezone.make_aware(value, project_tz)
    return value.astimezone(project_tz)


def _publish_date_as_local(value):
    """Interpret a publish_date value as local wall-clock time in the project timezone.

    Mirrors the convention in models.py (publish_dates_dict, due_dates_dict): stored
    values are treated as local wall-clock times in settings.TIME_ZONE, NOT converted
    from UTC.  Matches the .replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo(settings.TIME_ZONE)) pattern used
    throughout the codebase.
    """
    project_tz = ZoneInfo(settings.TIME_ZONE)
    return value.replace(tzinfo=project_tz)


def get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at):
    project_tz = ZoneInfo(settings.TIME_ZONE)
    occurred_local = _to_project_timezone(occurred_at)

    if assignment.recurrence_starts_on is not None:
        anchor_local = _to_project_timezone(assignment.recurrence_starts_on)
    elif assignment.publish_date is not None:
        # publish_date follows the codebase wall-clock convention: treat the stored
        # value as a local time in settings.TIME_ZONE, never convert from UTC.
        anchor_local = _publish_date_as_local(assignment.publish_date)
    else:
        anchor_local = occurred_local

    if assignment.recurrence_unit == assignment.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY:
        # Compute boundaries from the calendar date of occurred_local so that period
        # starts always land at midnight in the project timezone regardless of DST
        # transitions.  Fixed-offset timedelta stepping from a localized anchor would
        # drift by one hour across a DST boundary.
        period_date = occurred_local.date()
        next_date = period_date + timedelta(days=1)
        period_start = datetime(period_date.year, period_date.month, period_date.day, tzinfo=project_tz)
        period_end = datetime(next_date.year, next_date.month, next_date.day, tzinfo=project_tz)
    elif assignment.recurrence_unit == assignment.RECURRENCE_UNIT_WEEK:
        anchor_start = anchor_local
        unit = timedelta(days=7)
        period_index = math.floor((occurred_local - anchor_start) / unit)
        period_start = anchor_start + (period_index * unit)
        period_end = period_start + unit
    else:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported recurrence unit")

    return period_start.astimezone(project_tz), period_end.astimezone(project_tz)


def _is_error_free_attempt(attempt):
    error_tally = attempt.get("error_tally")
    if error_tally is None:
        return True
    try:
        return int(error_tally) == 0
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False


def _normalize_attempt_exercise_id(attempt):
    attempt_id = attempt.get("id")
    if attempt_id is None:
        return None
    return str(attempt_id)[:6]


def _build_remaining_requirements(exercise_ids):
    return set(exercise_ids)


def _parse_attempt_performed_at(value):
    if isinstance(value, datetime):
        return value
    return parse_datetime(str(value))


def count_playlist_cycles(exercise_ids, attempts, cap):
    if not exercise_ids or cap <= 0:
        return 0, None, None

    counted_passes = 0
    first_pass_at = None
    last_counted_pass_at = None
    remaining = _build_remaining_requirements(exercise_ids)

    for attempt in attempts:
        if counted_passes >= cap:
            break
        if not isinstance(attempt, dict):
            continue
        if not _is_error_free_attempt(attempt):
            continue

        completed_at = _parse_attempt_performed_at(attempt.get("performed_at"))
        if completed_at is None:
            continue

        normalized_exercise_id = _normalize_attempt_exercise_id(attempt)
        if normalized_exercise_id not in remaining:
            continue

        remaining.remove(normalized_exercise_id)

        if not remaining:
            counted_passes += 1
            if first_pass_at is None:
                first_pass_at = completed_at
            last_counted_pass_at = completed_at
            if counted_passes >= cap:
                break
            remaining = _build_remaining_requirements(exercise_ids)

    return counted_passes, first_pass_at, last_counted_pass_at


def rebuild_period_progress(assignment, performance_data, occurred_at):
    from apps.exercises.models import RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress

    period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)
    attempts_in_period = []
    for attempt in performance_data.data:
        if not isinstance(attempt, dict):
            continue

        parsed_performed_at = _parse_attempt_performed_at(attempt.get("performed_at"))
        if parsed_performed_at is None:
            continue

        # Historical performance payloads store naive timestamp strings that are
        # intended as UTC wall-clock values (e.g. "2026-04-09T04:00:00").
        if timezone.is_naive(parsed_performed_at):
            parsed_performed_at = timezone.make_aware(parsed_performed_at, dt_timezone.utc)

        performed_at_local = _to_project_timezone(parsed_performed_at)
        if period_start <= performed_at_local < period_end:
            attempt_for_counting = dict(attempt)
            attempt_for_counting["performed_at"] = performed_at_local
            attempts_in_period.append(attempt_for_counting)

    attempts_in_period.sort(key=lambda attempt: attempt["performed_at"])

    counted_passes, first_pass_at, last_counted_pass_at = count_playlist_cycles(
        performance_data.playlist.exercise_list,
        attempts_in_period,
        cap=assignment.required_passes_per_period,
    )

    progress, _ = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.update_or_create(
        user=performance_data.user,
        course=assignment.course,
        playlist=assignment.playlist,
        period_start=period_start,
        defaults={
            "period_end": period_end,
            "counted_passes": counted_passes,
            "required_passes": assignment.required_passes_per_period,
            "target_met": counted_passes >= assignment.required_passes_per_period,
            "first_pass_at": first_pass_at,
            "last_counted_pass_at": last_counted_pass_at,
        },
    )
    return progress


def get_recurring_assignment_snapshot(user, assignment, occurred_at=None):
    from apps.exercises.models import RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress

    occurred_at = occurred_at or timezone.now()
    period_start, period_end = get_assignment_period_bounds(assignment, occurred_at)

    current_progress = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        course=assignment.course,
        playlist=assignment.playlist,
        period_start=period_start,
    ).first()

    completed_periods = RecurringPlaylistPeriodProgress.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        course=assignment.course,
        playlist=assignment.playlist,
        target_met=True,
    ).count()

    counted_passes = current_progress.counted_passes if current_progress else 0
    required_passes = assignment.required_passes_per_period
    period_label = (
        "today"
        if assignment.recurrence_unit == assignment.RECURRENCE_UNIT_DAY
        else "this week"
    )
    target_met = counted_passes >= required_passes

    return {
        "is_recurring": True,
        "counted_passes": counted_passes,
        "required_passes": required_passes,
        "progress_label": f"{counted_passes} of {required_passes} {period_label}",
        "target_met": target_met,
        "completed_periods": completed_periods,
        "next_reset_at": period_end,
    }

apps/exercises/utils/transpose.py
File type: .py
# """
# Transpose exercise content per a new text field in playlist editor.
#
# User input example: `C G c#'
# Result: populate playlist with each exercise in 0, 1, 4 sharps
#
# The distinction of major and minor is immaterial; this is a convenient shorthand.
#
# Exercise ID will appear as EA00DD+16 or EA00DD-2 where you see the midi_vector.
#
# Options:
# (1) loop transpositions per exercise,
# (2) loop transpositions per playlist,
# (3) shuffle transpositions per exercise (pseudo-random),
# (4) shuffle transpositions per playlist (pseudo-random).
#
# That is:
# (1) A+1,A+2,A+3,B+1,B+2,B+3
# (2) A+1,B+1,A+2,B+2,A+3,B+3
# (3) A+2,A+1,A+3,B+1,B+3,B+2
# (4) A+3,B+1,B+3,A+2,B+2,A+1
# """
from copy import deepcopy

from apps.exercises.constants import sig_to_pc, pseudo_key_to_sig, all_sigs, all_keys


def transpose(exercise, staff_sig_request):
    exercise = deepcopy(exercise)
    sig_orig = exercise.data.get("keySignature")
    pc_ref_orig = sig_to_pc[sig_orig]
    key_orig = exercise.data.get("key")
    if staff_sig_request not in all_sigs:
        return exercise
        # Bogus requests should never get this far, due to Django validation
        # of tranpose_requests and tests in transposition_matrix.
        # If they did, returning the untransposed exercise more than once
        # would cause grading problems.

    pc_ref_target = sig_to_pc[staff_sig_request]

    if key_orig == "h":
        key_target = key_orig
    else:
        try:
            fifth_chain_move = all_sigs.index(staff_sig_request) - all_sigs.index(sig_orig)
            key_target = all_keys[all_keys.index(key_orig) + 2 * fifth_chain_move]
        except IndexError:
            return exercise
            # ditto comment on return statement above

    # 12 + not necessary here but keep it in case this function copied to Javascript
    pc_vector = (12 + pc_ref_target - pc_ref_orig) % 12

    midi_all_ex = []
    for chord in exercise.data["chord"]:
        midi_all_ex.extend(chord["visible"] + chord["hidden"])

    midi_max_ex = max(midi_all_ex)
    midi_min_ex = min(midi_all_ex)
    midi_mean_floor_ex = (midi_max_ex + midi_min_ex) // 2
    midi_range_ex = midi_max_ex + 1 - midi_min_ex

    # suitable for 88-key controllers, A0 to C8
    midi_mean_floor_target_min = 59
    if midi_range_ex <= 14:
        # suitable for 25-key controllers, C3 to C5
        midi_mean_floor_target_min = 54
    elif midi_range_ex <= 21:
        # suitable for 32-key controllers, 8vb, F2 to C5
        # Arturia, Midiplus, Native Instruments
        midi_mean_floor_target_min = 51
    elif midi_range_ex <= 26:
        # suitable for 37-key controllers, 8vb, C2 to C5
        midi_mean_floor_target_min = 48
    elif midi_range_ex <= 38:
        # suitable for 49-key controllers, C2 to C6
        midi_mean_floor_target_min = 54
    elif midi_range_ex <= 50:
        # suitable for 61-key controllers, C2 to C7
        midi_mean_floor_target_min = 60
    midi_mean_floor_target_range = range(
        midi_mean_floor_target_min, midi_mean_floor_target_min + 12
    )

    midi_vector = None

    if False:
        # TODO: enable this as an option in the playlist transposition controls
        # algorithm that fits exercise onto smallest standard keyboard
        # that will accommodate all keys
        octave_displ = 0
        arbitrary_limit = 7
        while octave_displ < arbitrary_limit and octave_displ > -arbitrary_limit:
            if (
                midi_mean_floor_ex + pc_vector + 12 * octave_displ
            ) in midi_mean_floor_target_range:
                midi_vector = pc_vector + 12 * octave_displ
                break
            if octave_displ >= 0:
                octave_displ += 1
            octave_displ *= -1
    else:
        # Pick the direction that results in the smaller interval (≤ 6 semitones).
        # For exactly 6 semitones (tritone), prefer going down.
        if pc_vector >= 6:
            midi_vector = pc_vector - 12  # go down instead
        else:
            midi_vector = pc_vector
    # TODO: allow additional transpose options (incl. define a lowest pseudo_key, set the lowest tenor note)

    if midi_vector == None:
        # No transposition operation was identified
        return exercise
        # ditto comment on return statement above

    # make the transposition
    for chord in exercise.data["chord"]:
        transposed = [note + midi_vector for note in chord["visible"]]
        chord.update(visible=transposed)

        transposed = [note + midi_vector for note in chord["hidden"]]
        chord.update(hidden=transposed)

    exercise.data["key"] = key_target
    exercise.data["keySignature"] = staff_sig_request

    exercise.id = f"{exercise.id}{midi_vector}"

    return exercise

function downloadCSV(csv, filename) {
    var csvFile;
    var downloadLink;

    // CSV file
    csvFile = new Blob([csv], {type: "text/csv"});

    // Download link
    downloadLink = document.createElement("a");

    // File name
    downloadLink.download = filename;

    // Create a link to the file
    downloadLink.href = window.URL.createObjectURL(csvFile);

    // Hide download link
    downloadLink.style.display = "none";

    // Add the link to DOM
    document.body.appendChild(downloadLink);

    // Click download link
    downloadLink.click();
}
function exportTableToCSV(filename, colcount=false) {
    var csv = [];
    var rows = document.querySelectorAll("table tr");

    for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
        var row = [], cols = rows[i].querySelectorAll("td, th");

        const col_limit = (colcount && colcount <= cols.length ? colcount : cols.length);
        for (var j = 0; j < col_limit; j++) {
            row.push(cols[j].innerText);
        }

        csv.push(row.join(","));
    }

    // Download CSV file
    downloadCSV(csv.join("\n"), filename);
}
</script>

# Key map: HarmonyLab key string → music21 key name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEY_MAP = {
    "jC_": "C",  "jG_": "G",  "jD_": "D",  "jA_": "A",  "jE_": "E",  "jB_": "B",
    "jF#": "F#", "jDb": "Db", "jAb": "Ab", "jEb": "Eb", "jBb": "Bb", "jF_": "F",
    "iA_": "a",  "iE_": "e",  "iB_": "b",  "iF#": "f#", "iC#": "c#", "iG#": "g#",
    "iD_": "d",  "iG_": "g",  "iC_": "c",  "iF_": "f",  "iBb": "bb", "iEb": "eb",
}

# KEY_SPELLING: Python mirror of general.js keyMap spelling arrays.
# Each entry maps pitch class (0–11) → note name string as HarmonyLab renders it.
# Used by spelling_key_for_pitches() to find the right exercise 'key' so that
# enharmonically-sensitive notes (e.g. A# vs Bb) display correctly on the staff.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

}

# Chord quality → list of interval strings above root

QUALITY_INTERVALS = {

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LABEL_MAP = {
    "triad": {
        "quality": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["major", "minor", "diminished", "augmented"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: quality,
        },
        "inversion": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["root position", "first inversion", "second inversion"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: ["root position", "first inversion", "second inversion"][inv],
        },
    },
    "seventh_chord": {
        "quality": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["dominant 7", "major 7", "minor 7", "half-dim 7", "diminished 7"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: {
                "dominant": "dominant 7", "major7": "major 7", "minor7": "minor 7",
                "half_dim": "half-dim 7", "dim7": "diminished 7",
            }.get(quality, quality),
        },
        "inversion": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["root position", "6/5", "4/3", "4/2"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: ["root position", "6/5", "4/3", "4/2"][inv],
        },
    },
    "interval": {
        "name": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["m2", "M2", "m3", "M3", "P4", "TT", "P5", "m6", "M6", "m7", "M7", "P8"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: quality,
        },
    },
    "diatonic_triads": {
        "roman_numeral": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["I", "ii", "iii", "IV", "V", "vi", "vii°"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: quality,
        },
    },
    "diatonic_sevenths": {
        "roman_numeral": {
            "choices": lambda k: ["Imaj7", "ii7", "iii7", "IVmaj7", "V7", "vi7", "viiø7"],
            "answer":  lambda quality, inv, k: quality,
        },
    },
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diatonic roman numeral sets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DIATONIC_TRIADS_MAJOR = ["I", "ii", "iii", "IV", "V", "vi", "vii°"]
DIATONIC_TRIADS_MINOR = ["i", "ii°", "III", "iv", "V", "VI", "VII"]

DIATONIC_SEVENTHS_MAJOR = ["Imaj7", "ii7", "iii7", "IVmaj7", "V7", "vi7", "viiø7"]
DIATONIC_SEVENTHS_MINOR = ["i7", "iiø7", "IIImaj7", "iv7", "V7", "VImaj7", "vii°7"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rule of the Octave chord sequences (roman numerals, ascending & descending)
# Bass walks diatonically; upper voices follow standard ROTO voice leading.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROTO_MAJOR_ASC = ["I", "V6/5", "I6", "V6/4/3", "V", "I6/4", "V4/3", "I"]   # sd 1-8
ROTO_MAJOR_DESC = ["I", "V4/2", "I6", "IV6", "V", "IV", "V6", "I"]            # sd 8-1
ROTO_MINOR_ASC  = ["i", "V6/5", "i6", "iv6/4/3", "V", "i6/4", "V4/3", "i"]
ROTO_MINOR_DESC = ["i", "V4/2", "i6", "iv6", "V", "iv", "V6", "i"]

# Simpler, more reliable RN strings for music21 ROTO:
ROTO_MAJOR_ASC_RN  = ["I",    "I6",   "I6",   "IV",   "V",    "I6/4", "VII6", "I"]
ROTO_MAJOR_DESC_RN = ["I",    "V7",   "I6",   "IV6",  "V",    "IV",   "V6",   "I"]
ROTO_MINOR_ASC_RN  = ["i",    "i6",   "i6",   "iv",   "V",    "i6/4", "VII6", "i"]
ROTO_MINOR_DESC_RN = ["i",    "V7",   "i6",   "iv6",  "V",    "iv",   "V6",   "i"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _m21_key(key_str: str):
    """Return a music21 Key object for the given HarmonyLab key string."""
    return m21_key.Key(KEY_MAP[key_str])


def spelling_key_for_pitches(m21_pitches, prefer_major: bool = True) -> str:
    """
    Given a list of music21 Pitch objects (with enharmonic spelling already set
    by music21 interval/roman logic), return the HarmonyLab key string whose
    keyMap spelling array renders all those pitches with the SAME note names.

    This lets you set exercise 'key' so notes display correctly regardless of
    whether the nominal key of the exercise would give the right spelling.
    Particularly useful for interval exercises with augmented/diminished intervals,
    or for any exercise where you want explicit control over accidentals.

    Usage in the management command:
        chords = mb.interval("jC_", "A6", "matching")
        pitches = mb._get_interval_pitches("jC_", "A6")   # helper below
        ex_key = mb.spelling_key_for_pitches(pitches)      # e.g. "jB_"
        exercise_json["key"] = ex_key
        exercise_json["keySignature"] = ""   # don't show a key signature

    Returns the first key (from a preference-ordered list) where all pitches
    match. Falls back to "jC_" if no perfect match is found.
    """
    # Convert pitch names: music21 uses '-' for flat (e.g. "D-"), keyMap uses 'b'
    def normalize(name: str) -> str:
        return name.replace("-", "b")

    target_spellings = {p.pitchClass: normalize(p.name) for p in m21_pitches}

    # Preference order: fewer accidentals first, major before minor
    preference = [
        "jC_", "jG_", "jF_", "jD_", "jBb", "jA_", "jEb", "jE_", "jAb",
        "jB_", "jDb", "jF#",
        "iA_", "iE_", "iD_", "iG_", "iB_", "iC_", "iF_", "iF#", "iBb",
        "iC#", "iG#", "iEb",
    ]

    for key_str in preference:
        spellings = KEY_SPELLING.get(key_str, [])
        if all(spellings[pc] == name for pc, name in target_spellings.items()):
            return key_str

    return "jC_"   # fallback


def _get_interval_pitches(key_str: str, interval_name: str):
    """
    Return the two music21 Pitch objects for an interval exercise (root + top).
    Exposed so the management command can call spelling_key_for_pitches() on them.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    root = k.tonic
    m21_name = "d5" if interval_name == "TT" else interval_name
    top = m21_interval.Interval(m21_name).transposePitch(root)
    return [root, top]


def _pitch_in_range(p: pitch.Pitch, midi_low: int, midi_high: int) -> pitch.Pitch:
    """
    Return a copy of `p` transposed to the nearest octave that falls within
    [midi_low, midi_high].  Raises ValueError if no such octave exists.
    """
    candidate = pitch.Pitch(p.name)          # strip octave info, keep spelling
    # start octave estimate from midi_low
    candidate.octave = (midi_low // 12) - 1  # MIDI 60 → octave 4 (C4=60)
    # step up until we're inside the window
    while candidate.midi < midi_low:
        candidate.octave += 1
    if candidate.midi > midi_high:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No spelling of {p.name} fits in MIDI range {midi_low}–{midi_high}"
        )
    return candidate


def _close_voice(pitches, inversion: int = 0):
    """
    Close voicing: all notes stacked tightly starting near MIDI 60.
    Returns list of pitch.Pitch objects.
    """
    rotated = list(pitches[inversion:]) + list(pitches[:inversion])
    bass = _pitch_in_range(rotated[0], 60, 71)
    notes = [bass]
    for p in rotated[1:]:
        note = _pitch_in_range(p, notes[-1].midi + 1, notes[-1].midi + 12)
        notes.append(note)
    return notes


def _keyboard_4voice(pitches, inversion: int = 0):
    """
    Keyboard voicing: bass in bass clef (MIDI 45–57), upper voices in
    treble clef (MIDI 60–76) close together.  For triads, doubles the root
    in the soprano.
    Returns list of pitch.Pitch objects.
    """
    root_pitch = pitches[0]
    rotated = list(pitches[inversion:]) + list(pitches[:inversion])
    bass = _pitch_in_range(rotated[0], 45, 57)

    upper = []
    prev_midi = 59
    for p in rotated[1:]:
        note = _pitch_in_range(p, prev_midi + 1, prev_midi + 12)
        upper.append(note)
        prev_midi = note.midi

    # For triads (3 distinct pitch classes) double the root in soprano
    if len(pitches) == 3:
        soprano = _pitch_in_range(root_pitch, prev_midi + 1, prev_midi + 12)
        upper.append(soprano)

    return [bass] + upper


def _voice(pitches, inversion: int, voicing_name: str):
    """Dispatch to the correct voicing strategy."""
    if voicing_name == "keyboard_4voice":
        return _keyboard_4voice(pitches, inversion)
    return _close_voice(pitches, inversion)


def _pitches_for_quality(root_pitch: pitch.Pitch, quality: str):
    """
    Build a list of pitch.Pitch objects for a chord quality rooted on
    root_pitch, using music21 intervals for correct enharmonic spelling.
    """
    ivl_names = QUALITY_INTERVALS.get(quality)
    if ivl_names is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown quality: {quality!r}")
    return [m21_interval.Interval(ivl).transposePitch(root_pitch) for ivl in ivl_names]


def _pitches_from_rn(rn_str: str, k) -> list:
    """
    Return the pitches of a RomanNumeral as a list of pitch.Pitch.
    music21's roman module handles enharmonic spelling relative to the key.
    """
    rn = roman.RomanNumeral(rn_str, k)
    return list(rn.pitches)


def _apply_visibility(midi_notes: list, exercise_type: str):
    """Split midi_notes into (visible, hidden) based on exercise type."""
    if exercise_type in ("matching", "identification"):
        return midi_notes, []
    elif exercise_type == "analytical":
        return [], midi_notes
    elif exercise_type in ("figured_bass", "figured_bass_pcs"):
        return [midi_notes[0]], midi_notes[1:]
    return midi_notes, []


def _chord_dict(
    midi_notes: list,
    rhythm_value: str,
    exercise_type: str,
    identification_label: str = None,
    key_str: str = None,
    quality: str = None,
    inversion: int = 0,
    exercise_category: str = None,
    rn_answer: str = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Build a single chord dict in the format expected by Exercise.data["chord"].
    """
    visible, hidden = _apply_visibility(sorted(midi_notes), exercise_type)
    d = {"visible": visible, "hidden": hidden, "rhythmValue": rhythm_value}

    if (
        exercise_type == "identification"
        and identification_label
        and exercise_category in LABEL_MAP
    ):
        label_info = LABEL_MAP[exercise_category].get(identification_label)
        if label_info:
            d["choices"] = label_info["choices"](key_str)
            if exercise_category in ("triad", "seventh_chord"):
                d["answer"] = label_info["answer"](quality, inversion, key_str)
            elif exercise_category == "interval":
                d["answer"] = label_info["answer"](quality, inversion, key_str)
            elif rn_answer is not None:
                d["answer"] = label_info["answer"](rn_answer, inversion, key_str)

    return d


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API — same signatures as the old templates.py
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def triad(key_str, quality, inversion, voicing_name, exercise_type,
          identification_label=None):
    """
    Single triad.
    Returns [{"visible": [...], "hidden": [...], "rhythmValue": "w"}].
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    pitches = _pitches_for_quality(k.tonic, quality)
    voiced = _voice(pitches, inversion, voicing_name)
    midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
    return [_chord_dict(
        midi_notes, "w", exercise_type,
        identification_label, key_str, quality, inversion, "triad",
    )]


def seventh_chord(key_str, quality, inversion, voicing_name, exercise_type,
                  identification_label=None):
    """
    Single seventh chord.
    Returns [{"visible": [...], "hidden": [...], "rhythmValue": "w"}].
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    pitches = _pitches_for_quality(k.tonic, quality)
    voiced = _voice(pitches, inversion, voicing_name)
    midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
    return [_chord_dict(
        midi_notes, "w", exercise_type,
        identification_label, key_str, quality, inversion, "seventh_chord",
    )]


def interval(key_str, interval_name, exercise_type, identification_label=None):
    """
    Single harmonic interval from the tonic.
    Returns [{"visible": [bottom_midi, top_midi], "hidden": [], "rhythmValue": "h"}].

    Accepts any music21 interval name: "m2","M2","m3","M3","P4","d5"/"TT","P5",
    "m6","M6","m7","M7","P8", and augmented/diminished variants like "A2","A3",
    "A4","A5","A6","d3","d4","d7" etc.

    NOTE — enharmonic display constraint: HarmonyLab's frontend uses a 12-element
    keyMap (general.js) that assigns ONE spelling per pitch class per key. MIDI
    numbers carry no spelling information. So augmented intervals will only display
    with the expected accidental if the active key's keyMap happens to spell that
    pitch class accordingly. For example, a C→A# (A6) in key jC_ will render as
    C→Bb (m7) because jC_ spells PC 10 as "Bb". Augmented intervals intended to
    display correctly should be used only in keys where the target pitch class is
    spelled as desired, or paired with a custom key context that spells it that way.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    root = k.tonic

    # "TT" (tritone) → diminished fifth for enharmonic-correct music21 spelling
    m21_name = "d5" if interval_name == "TT" else interval_name

    top = m21_interval.Interval(m21_name).transposePitch(root)
    p1 = _pitch_in_range(root, 60, 71)
    p2 = _pitch_in_range(top, p1.midi + 1, p1.midi + 12)

    return [_chord_dict(
        [p1.midi, p2.midi], "h", exercise_type,
        identification_label, key_str, interval_name, 0, "interval",
    )]


def diatonic_intervals(key_str, scale_type, exercise_type,
                       identification_label=None):
    """
    All 7 diatonic intervals above the tonic (M2 through P8).
    Returns list of 7 chord dicts.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    if scale_type == "major" or key_str.startswith("j"):
        sc = m21_scale.MajorScale(k.tonic)
    else:
        sc = m21_scale.NaturalMinorScale(k.tonic)

    # sc.pitches returns 8 pitches: root through octave (inclusive)
    all_pitches = sc.pitches   # e.g. [C4, D4, E4, F4, G4, A4, B4, C5]
    root = _pitch_in_range(k.tonic, 60, 71)
    chords = []
    # Intervals: 2nd through octave = indices 1–7 (7 intervals total)
    for sp in all_pitches[1:]:
        top = _pitch_in_range(sp, root.midi + 1, root.midi + 12)
        chords.append(_chord_dict([root.midi, top.midi], "h", exercise_type))
    return chords


def scale(key_str, scale_type, direction, exercise_type):
    """
    Scale as one note per chord dict.
    Returns list of 8 chord dicts (root to octave).
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    if scale_type == "major":
        sc = m21_scale.MajorScale(k.tonic)
    elif scale_type in ("harmonic_minor", "harmonic"):
        sc = m21_scale.HarmonicMinorScale(k.tonic)
    elif scale_type in ("melodic_minor", "melodic"):
        sc = m21_scale.MelodicMinorScale(k.tonic)
    else:
        sc = m21_scale.NaturalMinorScale(k.tonic)

    # sc.pitches gives 8 pitches: root to octave inclusive
    pitches = list(sc.pitches)   # 8 notes already

    if direction in ("descending", "desc"):
        pitches = list(reversed(pitches))

    chords = []
    for p in pitches:
        placed = _pitch_in_range(p, 60, 72)
        chords.append(_chord_dict([placed.midi], "q", exercise_type))
    return chords


def diatonic_triads(key_str, scale_type, exercise_type,
                    identification_label=None):
    """
    All 7 diatonic triads in keyboard_4voice voicing.
    Returns list of 7 chord dicts.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    is_major = key_str.startswith("j")
    rn_list = DIATONIC_TRIADS_MAJOR if is_major else DIATONIC_TRIADS_MINOR
    chords = []
    for rn_str in rn_list:
        pitches = _pitches_from_rn(rn_str, k)
        voiced = _keyboard_4voice(pitches, 0)
        midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
        chords.append(_chord_dict(
            midi_notes, "w", exercise_type,
            identification_label, key_str, None, 0,
            "diatonic_triads", rn_str,
        ))
    return chords


def diatonic_sevenths(key_str, scale_type, exercise_type,
                      identification_label=None):
    """
    All 7 diatonic seventh chords in keyboard_4voice voicing.
    Returns list of 7 chord dicts.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    is_major = key_str.startswith("j")
    rn_list = DIATONIC_SEVENTHS_MAJOR if is_major else DIATONIC_SEVENTHS_MINOR
    chords = []
    for rn_str in rn_list:
        pitches = _pitches_from_rn(rn_str, k)
        voiced = _keyboard_4voice(pitches, 0)
        midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
        chords.append(_chord_dict(
            midi_notes, "w", exercise_type,
            identification_label, key_str, None, 0,
            "diatonic_sevenths", rn_str,
        ))
    return chords


def roto(key_str, scale_type, direction, exercise_type):
    """
    Rule of the Octave: bass walks the scale, upper voices follow ROTO.
    Returns list of 8 chord dicts.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    is_major = key_str.startswith("j")

    if is_major:
        rn_list = ROTO_MAJOR_ASC_RN if direction in ("ascending", "asc") else ROTO_MAJOR_DESC_RN
    else:
        rn_list = ROTO_MINOR_ASC_RN if direction in ("ascending", "asc") else ROTO_MINOR_DESC_RN

    chords = []
    for rn_str in rn_list:
        pitches = _pitches_from_rn(rn_str, k)
        voiced = _keyboard_4voice(pitches, 0)
        midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
        chords.append(_chord_dict(midi_notes, "h", exercise_type))
    return chords


def progression(key_str, rn_list, exercise_type):
    """
    Chord progression expressed as roman numeral strings.
    Returns list of chord dicts, one per roman numeral.
    """
    k = _m21_key(key_str)
    chords = []
    for rn_str in rn_list:
        pitches = _pitches_from_rn(rn_str, k)
        voiced = _keyboard_4voice(pitches, 0)
        midi_notes = [p.midi for p in voiced]
        chords.append(_chord_dict(midi_notes, "w", exercise_type))
    return chords
